| D0136 | A | `lineage` classifies every atom it cannot resolve, and propagates the one error that is not a resolution failure | docs/specs/m2.md §7 requires `lineage` to be TOTAL: "an atom that does not resolve is classified, never raised on". Totality has to be given a boundary, because `Store.get_value` can fail three ways and they are not the same failure. . CLASSIFIED as `kind="unresolved"`: (1) `MissingRef` — nothing is stored at that ref. This is the case §7 names, and §6's absence witness is why it is not hypothetical: an anti-join cites a relation's content address and nothing guarantees that relation was ever stored. (2) `CanonicalEncodingError` — bytes are stored, and they are not a value. `Store.put_bytes` legitimately holds raw bytes (a source's own bytes are stored that way), so a ref can address something real that is nevertheless not a `srcrow/1` and not a `rel/1` and not anything else with a decodable canonical form. The taxonomy has three kinds and none of them is "bytes I cannot read", so this is the honest one: nothing here resolves to a value lineage can describe. . PROPAGATED: `IntegrityError` — bytes at rest that no longer hash to the ref they are filed under. This is not a citation failing to resolve; it is the store reporting that its own contract has been broken, which `Store.get_bytes` verifies on every read precisely so it can be noticed. Classifying it as `"unresolved"` would launder detected tampering into "not found" inside the one read a reader is most likely to trust — a serve-layer lineage view — and would make the store's verify-on-read pointless exactly where it matters most. A lineage read that raises here is a lineage read that has found something no caller can handle by carrying on. . The narrow reading of "total" — never raises, ever — was considered and rejected for that reason. Totality here is a property of the CITATION (every atom gets a classification), not a promise that the storage layer underneath is functioning. . A fourth kind for a malformed atom is not needed and is not added: `Why.of` refuses a non-ref by name, so a malformed atom cannot reach a `Rel` and therefore cannot reach here (L2.7 checks that rather than asserting it). | accepted | — | — | pytest: `tests/laws/m2/test_l2_lineage.py::test_l2_7_an_atom_that_is_not_in_the_store_is_classified_not_raised_on`; pytest: `tests/laws/m2/test_l2_lineage.py::test_l2_7_an_atom_outside_the_pinned_grammar_is_unconstructible`; file: `src/tannen/sources.py` |

| D0146 | A | Two ways an ad-hoc run leaks into a guarded one: an inherited TANNEN_ variable (fixed) and a .pyc in a sealed directory (queued, because the guard that catches it is the trust root) | Both were found the same way — by running commands against this repo during the M2 sitting-materials pass and watching guards report failures that were mine rather than the code's. Both are the same family: ambient process state reaching into a run that believes it controls its own conditions. One is fixed here; one is queued, with its mitigation written down. . (1) FIXED — `tests/test_laws_runner.py` inherited the environment it meant to override. `run_pytest` built its child env as `dict(os.environ, TANNEN_EVIDENCE_ROOT=…)`: inherit everything, override one. An ambient `TANNEN_NO_EVIDENCE=1` — exactly what someone sets so an ad-hoc run does not dirty `evidence/` — rode into the child, the plugin wrote nothing, and FOUR tests failed asserting records that were never going to exist. Every one of those failures names the harness, so they read as a regression in it while the cause is outside the process entirely. Observed, not hypothesised: it cost a round trip during this session. . The cure is the one this repo already owns for a different family. `scripts/_gov.py`'s `git_env()` strips `GIT_LOCATION_VARS` because `GIT_DIR` beats `git -C`, and the rule it encodes is: SCRUB THE FAMILY, THEN SET EXACTLY WHAT YOU MEAN. `child_env()` now does that for `TANNEN_EVIDENCE_ROOT`, `TANNEN_NO_EVIDENCE` and `TANNEN_CHECK_DECISIONS_NESTED`, at all three sites that spawn a pytest subprocess — including the two that deliberately SET one of them, because a test that says what it needs must not also inherit the negation. . `test_the_harness_scrubs_an_ambient_tannen_variable` constructs the hostile state (D0092): it sets the variable in its own process for the duration rather than trusting nobody will. Watched failing against the inheriting spelling and passing against the scrub. . THE GATE WAS NEVER SILENTLY WEAKENED BY THIS, which is worth stating so the fix is not read as larger than it is: with `TANNEN_NO_EVIDENCE=1` ambient, `make verify`'s pytest writes nothing and the very next step, `tannen laws report`, fails on missing evidence. It fails loudly. The damage was confined to spurious failures in one test file. . (2) QUEUED — `scripts/custodian.sh:66` and `scripts/check_manifest.py:113` disagree about `__pycache__`. The custodian enumerates `$(find tests/poison -type f | sort)` and requires a manifest row for every result, with no exclusion; `check_manifest.check_sealed_paths` skips any path with `__pycache__` in its parts, by name. So a `.pyc` written into `tests/poison/oracle-shadow/` — which happens on any import from that directory without `-B` or `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` — leaves `check_manifest` green and the custodian red. Reproduced: this session's own manual runs of the oracle-shadow reproduction did exactly that, and `make verify` failed at its LAST step after 37 minutes with "custodian: FAIL — not manifested: …/bootstrap_shadow.cpython-313-pytest-9.1.1.pyc". . THE MESSAGE INVITES THE WRONG FIX, and that is what makes it worth recording rather than just cleaning up. "not manifested: <path>" reads as "add a manifest row", and a manifest row for a `.pyc` would be wrong twice over: the file is gitignored, and its name carries the interpreter version, so the row would break on the next Python. The only correct response is to delete the file, which the message does not say. . NOT FIXED HERE because `scripts/custodian.sh` is the trust root and author-key territory (CLAUDE.md hard rules, BRIEF §9.1): only the owner edits it. Queued for M3 rather than added to the M2 driver, which is already 1468 lines and whose step 6 would need a newly tuned custodian copy for a one-line exclusion. THE MITIGATION IS FREE AND IS WRITTEN DOWN: every in-repo runner already does the right thing — `tests/test_governance_scripts.py`'s poison matrix sets `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` and its oracle-shadow tests pass `-B` — so the hazard is reachable only from ad-hoc commands. Do not import from `tests/poison/` without `-B`. . ONE THING THE SITTING SHOULD KNOW: the driver's `unexpected_failures()` does NOT tolerate a "not manifested:" line, so if this debris is present when the owner starts, step 0's gate stops the sitting over a stray `.pyc`. `find tests/poison -name __pycache__ -type d` before running is a five-second precaution. | accepted | — | governance-paths | pytest: `tests/test_laws_runner.py::test_the_harness_scrubs_an_ambient_tannen_variable`; file: `tests/test_laws_runner.py`; manifest: `scripts/custodian.sh` |
| D0147 | A | Three defects in the M2 sitting driver that only executing it could find: a binding orphaned by the fixture it names, a guard patch that reddens a test file it never mentions, and a projection left stale by the two steps that run after it | The M2 driver was read closely, step by step, and every new step was applied in a sandbox and watched refusing a second application (D0143). All three defects below survived all of that and were found by rehearsing the finished driver end to end — one per run, each deeper than the last, because a rehearsal only tests as far as it gets. None is exotic; all three are the same shape — a step's blast radius reaching past the file it edits, to a file it does not name. . (1) A BINDING THAT NAMED THE FIXTURE'S CANDIDATE PATH DIED WHEN STEP 5 MOVED IT. Found by the first rehearsal, which exited 1 at step 5 with ten failed post-conditions. D0141 binds `docs/redteam/fixture-candidates/oracle-shadow-model/README.md`. Step 5 `git mv`s that directory into `tests/poison/`, and the driver's own post-move guard — written for exactly this, twenty lines below the move — stopped the sitting with "a decision binding stopped resolving when the fixtures moved". The guard was right. The sitting stopping was not: the repair is mechanical, it is builder work, and it belongs in the same breath as the move that causes it rather than in the owner's lap five steps in. . FIXED BY RETARGETING, NOT DROPPING. At M1 the same shape was answered by deleting the binding before the sitting (D0104's note, quoted in step 5b). That is a real answer and a lossy one: `tests/poison/` is sealed and manifested, so a binding on the installed path still names a file whose removal turns `check_manifest` red, where a dropped binding names nothing. Step 5 now retargets it, correcting the `detail`'s tense in the same replacement — "staged outside tests/poison/" stops being true the instant the `git mv` lands, and a true future tense left standing becomes a false present one, which is the correction step 4h makes to D0110 for the same reason. Guarded on the directory AND on the old path still being present, so it is inert on a resumed sitting and on a declined install. . THIS IS BUILDER WORK BECAUSE OF A FACT ABOUT D0141 SPECIFICALLY, not a general licence: it is Tier A and unsigned. Were it Tier C and signed, D0063 ruling 2 would make its bindings as immutable as its text and the edit and the re-signature would have to be one act — the shape step 4h uses. . (2) STEP 4g'S GUARD PATCH TURNS FOUR CASES OF A TEST FILE IT NEVER MENTIONS RED. Found by the same run, as two of the four violations at step 5's post-move check. `tests/test_tier_c_signatures.py` is hermetic: it builds a throwaway tree and writes a `DECISIONS.md` that is a bare `input_hash` header, with a comment saying projection freshness is not what those tests are about. RT-M2-05's fix gives the projection a SECOND thing it must carry — the attention-receipt line the run computes, because the hash cannot see the clock — so a bare header stopped being a fresh projection the moment the patch landed. Four of the file's seven cases assert exit 0; all four went red. D0063 and D0064 both bind that file, which is how the rehearsal surfaced it. . Left as drafted, step 4g would have closed the M2 boundary on a red suite — the gate at step 9 would have failed, after five signatures and a receipt. . THE FIXTURE IS CORRECTED IN THE SAME EDIT, from `receipt_state` — the function the guard itself calls — so a throwaway tree with no `receipts/` states the STALE verdict it actually has rather than faking a FRESH one. The alternative, letting the guard pass when the projection carries no receipt line at all, was rejected: it reopens the hole RT-M2-05 named, since `DECISIONS.md`'s own bytes are not an input to the hash that guards it, so deleting the line would become the evasion. `tests/test_tier_c_signatures.py` is neither frozen nor custody-set, so it needs no signature; it lands beside the guard because landing it separately means landing it red. Same shape as step 4f (the Makefile and its docstring) and step 4i (the schema, the check and the test). . (3) THE PROJECTION IS STALE AT THE CLOSING GATE, BECAUSE BOTH OF ITS CLOCK-DEPENDENT INPUTS ARRIVE AFTER THE LAST STEP THAT REGENERATED IT. Found by the third rehearsal, the first to survive far enough to reach the close: eight post-conditions green — receipt taken and signed, `m2-close` minted and verifying as `owner@tannen`, custody set signed, custodian green with no tolerances — and then step 11's `make verify` red, with "DECISIONS.md's attention-receipt line is not what today computes". `DECISIONS.md` was last generated at the top of step 9. Step 9's custodian then writes `receipts/<today>.md` and step 10 mints the close tag, and BOTH are inputs to the freshness verdict, so the projection asserts the PREVIOUS boundary's window while the run computes this one's. The second violation in that gate — `tests/test_governance_scripts.py` — was a cascade of the first, since that file runs `check_decisions` against the real tree. . THIS IS RT-M2-05'S OWN FINDING, REAPPEARING INSIDE THE DRIVER THAT FIXES IT, and that is the argument for the fix rather than an irony. Before step 4g's check existed nothing could say the projection was stale, so every prior sitting simply carried the staleness into its closing commit — which is precisely the state the red team found in the tree M1 left behind. The new check found it on its first outing, in the one place the builder had not thought to look. . FIXED BY REGENERATING IN STEP 11, immediately before the closing gate, because there is no earlier point at which both inputs exist. Neither `DECISIONS.md` nor `CONCEPTS.md` is in `MANIFEST.sha256` or in the custody set — checked against both files, not assumed — so the regeneration disturbs no seal and invalidates no signature, and step 11's own commit picks the result up. The alternative of regenerating after the sitting was rejected because it is what was already nominally true and what failed: `docs/SITTING.md` listed "regenerate the projections" under work for the builder afterwards, which means the boundary commit is sealed and tagged around a projection known to be wrong. That line is the habit that caused this, and it has been removed. . VERIFIED FROM THE FAILING SIDE, all three items, per `produce-the-failure`. (1) was watched stopping a rehearsal, and the corrected step was watched applying its diff and the same check then passing on to step 5b in a live run. (2) was reproduced locally in the order that proves it: guard patched and fixture NOT -> 4 failed / 3 passed, each failure naming the missing attention-receipt line; fixture patched -> 7 passed. The guard itself was then checked both ways on the real tree — exit 0 today, and exit 1 at `--today 2026-09-08` with four violations naming the header and D0006/D0014/D0020, which is precisely what step 4g's own note text promises. (3) was reproduced in the rehearsal clone kept frozen in the state the failure left it: `check_decisions` red on the attention-receipt line, then `gen_projections.py`, then `check_decisions: OK — 146 records valid, DECISIONS.md fresh`. That clone's full `make verify` was then run to completion — green end to end, 716 passed / 1 skipped / 1 xfailed, custodian green, custody floor intact — which is what establishes that the second violation was a cascade of the first and not a separate defect. . NOT A DEFECT, AND WORTH KNOWING BEFORE THE NEXT RUN: step 5's post-move check reports two violations mid-sitting — a stale `DECISIONS.md` (step 4 edited decision records, so the input hash has legitimately moved and step 9 regenerates) and `tests/test_governance_scripts.py` failing on the dirty tree. Two is the expected noise at that point. | D0148 | A | D0147's item 3 names the wrong input, and the decline path's stop is the guard working: what rehearsing the M2 driver from a clean HEAD corrected | The `--from head --answers n` rehearsal — the first run ever to enter the driver with a clean tree — corrected one claim in D0147 and settled two questions about the decline path. This is a NEW record rather than an edit to D0147 because D0045 makes a decision's fields immutable and no guard enforces that; the record of the mistake is part of the record. . (1) THE CORRECTION. D0147 item 3 says the projection is stale at the closing gate because "BOTH of the projection's clock-dependent inputs arrived after it", and that `DECISIONS.md` "was last generated at the top of step 9". Both halves are wrong, and in the same way: step 9 regenerates TWICE. `gen_projections.py` runs at its top (`boundary_sitting.sh:1817`) and `make digest` runs at its end (`:1822`), after `custodian.sh` has written and signed `receipts/<today>.md`. So the receipt IS accounted for by the time step 9 ends. THE CLOSE TAG IS THE SOLE INPUT THAT ARRIVES AFTER THE LAST REGENERATION, minted by step 10. . THE EVIDENCE IS A CLONE STOPPED IN EXACTLY THAT STATE. The decline run halted at step 10 with the receipt written and signed, `make digest` run, and no close tag; its `DECISIONS.md:10` reads "receipt 2026-09-01.md fresh (no milestone boundary since)". `_gov.py:300-306` takes that branch when no boundary tag is dated on or after the receipt, and the "fresh until <d+7> (boundary <d> + 7d)" branch once one is — and the latter string, naming 2026-09-01, is precisely what the third rehearsal's step-11 failure quoted as what today computes. One input, not two. . THE FIX D0147 DESCRIBES IS UNCHANGED AND THIS SHARPENS ITS ARGUMENT rather than weakening it. Step 11's regeneration is not merely the earliest convenient point; it is the first opportunity after the only missing input exists, since the tag is minted at step 10 and step 11 is the next step. What is now known to be unnecessary is any worry about the receipt: D0147's "no earlier point where both inputs exist" reasoning arrives at the right placement for a reason that is half wrong, and a future reader moving that regeneration earlier on the strength of it would break the fix. Hence this record. . (2) THE COVERAGE GAP IS CLOSED. `--from worktree` can never reach `RESUMED=0` — the harness dirties four tracked files before the driver starts — so until this run, step 0's precondition gate and the RT-M2-06 D1 `else` branch had never executed in any rehearsal, including the green one banked before the seven new steps. This run entered with a clean tree: no "so this is a RESUMED sitting" note, no stray-dirt note, the gate offered and declined. The branch that decides resumption from sitting-shaped artifacts only, rather than from any dirt at all, is now exercised rather than reasoned about. . (3) THE DECLINE PATH IS NOT CHEAP, AND THE PLAN SAID IT WOULD BE. It took 3522 seconds — 59 minutes — because declining step 0's gate does not avoid step 9's, which is not behind a `confirm` (`:1819`). Neither are the regeneration, the custodian, or the digest; only the commit is. A decline run therefore costs about what an accept run costs, and the reason to run one is coverage, never speed. . (4) ITS STOP IS THE GUARD WORKING, NOT A FOURTH DEFECT. Because step 9's writes are unconditional and its commit is not, answering `n` throughout leaves a modified `DECISIONS.md` and an untracked signed receipt and digest. Step 10 then refuses: "the tree is not clean, so m2-close would attest a commit that does not contain this sitting's work — and would quote working-tree hashes absent from it (D0051)". That is exactly the property RT-M2-06 D2 was written to restore, firing correctly, before any tag was signed. The harness's two failed checks — "ran to completion" and "no step aborted" — are accept-path expectations that do not apply to a full decline, and the run is read as green on the question it was launched to answer. . (5) OBSERVED AND DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED BEFORE THE SITTING: a declined sitting is not a no-op. `custodian.sh` writes and signs the receipt before the owner is asked to commit anything, so abandoning a decline leaves a signed receipt untracked — and step 0 clause (b) reads untracked `receipts/` as sitting artifacts, making the NEXT run `RESUMED=1` and skipping the precondition gate. Every part of that is correct on its own terms: a receipt does exist, and the resumed branch announces itself rather than acting silently. It is recorded because "I ran it and declined everything" leaves state behind, which is not what a reader would assume, and because moving the receipt behind a confirm is a change to the order the receipt-then-tag argument depends on (D0071) — not something to attempt six days before the deadline, on the strength of a path the owner will not take. | accepted | — | governance-paths | file: `decisions/0147-three-defects-only-running-the-driver-could-find.yaml`; file: `docs/proposals/2026-08-31-m2-boundary-sitting/boundary_sitting.sh`; file: `scripts/_gov.py`; file: `scripts/rehearse_sitting.sh` |
| D0149 | A | The rehearsal verdict read the clock twice and called a signed receipt missing: a midnight-crossing defect in the harness, not the driver | `scripts/rehearse_sitting.sh` asserted the sitting's attention receipt by recomputing the date at verdict time — `test -f "$CLONE/receipts/$(date +%F).md"` and the matching `.sig`. That is a SECOND reading of a clock the driver already read, hours earlier, inside `custodian.sh`. Replaced both checks with a snapshot-and-difference: capture the clone's receipts before the driver starts (`RECEIPTS_BEFORE`, taken beside `CLOSE_TAG_PREEXISTED`) and let the verdict ask which receipt THIS RUN ADDED. . WHAT IT COST TO FIND. The `--from head --answers y` rehearsal began 2026-09-01 21:36 and its custodian wrote and signed `receipts/2026-09-01.md` at 23:23. The verdict ran after midnight, computed `2026-09-02`, and printed FAIL twice — "this sitting took a fresh attention receipt" and "and signed it" — against a clone where both were true and the files were sitting on disk, signed, committed, and covered by a green custodian run. . THIS IS THE HARNESS, NOT THE DRIVER, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE POINT. The driver ran to completion (exit 0), aborted no step, minted `m2-close` and verified it as owner@tannen, signed the custody set, and left the custodian green with no tolerances. Nothing about the sitting it rehearsed was wrong. So this defect does NOT invalidate the driver evidence from runs 4 and 5, and does not trigger the "re-run all three paths" rule that a DRIVER edit triggers — that rule exists because a run stops at its first failure, and no run stopped here. . THE REAL SITTING WAS NEVER AT RISK, and it is worth saying why rather than assuming it. `date +%F` appeared exactly twice in the harness and nowhere in the driver's assertions: `custodian.sh` names the receipt once, and everything downstream — `check_receipts.py`, `receipt_state` in `_gov.py` — reads the LATEST receipt off the directory rather than recomputing a name. An owner sitting that crosses midnight therefore behaves correctly; only the rehearsal's scorecard was wrong. . AND A SELF-INFLICTED ONE, RECORDED BECAUSE IT NEARLY COST THE EVIDENCE. This fix was applied to `rehearse_sitting.sh` WHILE run 5 was still executing that same file. `bash` reads a script incrementally by byte offset rather than parsing it whole, so inserting ten lines shifted every offset after them and the running shell resumed mid-construct: `rehearse_sitting.sh: line 326: syntax error near unexpected token '('`. The file was never invalid — `bash -n` passes on it — but the run died after its last check and before `say "Unexpected failure lines in the transcript"`, losing that section and the final tally. Both were recoverable ONLY because `--keep` had preserved the transcript, and were re-derived by running the harness's own awk program against it: one line, `check_decisions: FAIL (2 violation(s))` at step 5, which is the expected mid-sitting pair D0147 already documents as NOT a defect. THE RULE: never edit a shell script that is currently running. Copy it, edit the copy, and swap it in after the run exits. | accepted | — | governance-paths | file: `scripts/rehearse_sitting.sh`; file: `docs/proposals/2026-08-31-m2-boundary-sitting/boundary_sitting.sh` |
| D0150 | A | The branch that carries the owner's first command was the one branch never rehearsed: the harness erased the custody drift it was supposed to reproduce | `scripts/rehearse_sitting.sh` copied the driver under test into the clone's `scripts/boundary_sitting.sh` and only AFTERWARDS ran `gen_custody.py` and re-signed `governance/custody.sha256`. Because that path is a custody-set member, regenerating after the copy folded the new driver's bytes into the custody set — so the clone had no drift, step 0's gate was green, and the branch that tolerates the drift never executed. The `cp` is now DEFERRED until after the custody set is generated and signed, which reproduces the owner's real starting state in both modes. . WHAT THE OWNER ACTUALLY DOES, AND WHY IT WAS UNTESTED. The sitting begins `cp docs/proposals/<…>/boundary_sitting.sh scripts/` against a custody set the owner signed at the LAST sitting, over the PREVIOUS milestone's driver. That copy is custody drift by construction: the gate is red from the owner's first command, and step 0 continues only because `unexpected_failures()` tolerates that one drift by name until step 7 re-signs. Six rehearsals passed without once running it — `grep -c "green except the custody set"` over all four kept transcripts returns 0. . THE TOLERANCE WAS THEN VERIFIED DIRECTLY, because a fix that assumes the branch works is the same mistake one layer up. The drift state was reproduced in the kept run-6 clone and the real guards were run against it: `check_manifest` emits `custody drift: scripts/boundary_sitting.sh changed since the custody file was written` under a `check_manifest: FAIL (1 violation(s))` header, and the custodian emits `custody set hashes do not verify` and `custody floor violated`. Feeding that captured output to the driver's own `unexpected_failures()` returns EMPTY, so step 0 prints "green except the custody set, which is this sitting's step 7 — continuing". The branch is correct. It had simply never been executed, which is a different fact and the one worth fixing. . ORDERING CONSTRAINT, since two properties compete. The copy must land AFTER the custody signing (or there is no drift to rehearse) and BEFORE head mode's fixture commit (or the copy is uncommitted, the tree is dirty, and `RESUMED=0` — the branch D0148 bought — is lost again). The single insertion point that satisfies both is between them. . `docs/SITTING.md` carried the matching documentation defect and is corrected in the same pass: its driver line read `bash scripts/boundary_sitting.sh [milestone]` with no `cp`, while `scripts/boundary_sitting.sh` holds the M1 driver — a 1216-line divergence that a driver would not announce, because it takes its milestone from the argument. . AND THE FIX IS VERIFIABLE FROM ONLY ONE MODE, which is worth stating because getting it wrong cost a run. On a RESUMED sitting step 0 does not run the gate at all — it says the precondition gate "would read red for this sitting's own doing" and defers to step 9 — so the tolerance branch is unreachable there. `--from worktree` ALWAYS reports RESUMED, because the harness's own fixture edits dirty the tree before the driver starts (D0148). The drift-tolerance branch is therefore reachable ONLY from `--from head`. A worktree run launched to confirm this fix is a test whose outcome cannot depend on the fix — the exact error this record names, committed while recording it. | accepted | — | governance-paths | file: `scripts/rehearse_sitting.sh`; file: `docs/SITTING.md` |
| D0151 | A | Step 0's precondition gate cannot run once the cp that precedes it has happened: the sitting's founding assurance is established before the copy or not at all | The owner must run `make verify` BEFORE copying the milestone's driver into `scripts/`, not after. `docs/SITTING.md` and the M2 proposal README are corrected to put the gate first and to say why step 0's own offer cannot substitute for it. . WHAT THE HEAD-MODE REHEARSAL SHOWED. With the harness fixed to reproduce the owner's real starting state (D0150), step 0's gate ran for the first time against a drifted tree — and finished in ZERO SECONDS. `check_manifest.py` is the first recipe line of the `verify` target (`Makefile:35`); the cp is custody drift on `scripts/boundary_sitting.sh`; the check fails, `make` stops, and `check_concepts`, `check_decisions`, `check_tag_signers`, `check_receipts`, **the entire pytest suite**, `tannen laws report` and `lint-imports` never execute. The driver then prints "green except the custody set, which is this sitting's step 7 — continuing". . THAT SENTENCE IS TRUE AND READS AS SOMETHING STRONGER. `unexpected_failures()` correctly found nothing but the tolerated drift, because nothing else got the chance to fail. The owner sees a `waiting` line promising 35-40 minutes, an immediate return, and a reassuring note — the shape of a gate that ran and was green apart from one expected complaint. No gate ran. On the accept path the sitting then proceeds to step 9 before any suite executes. . THE FIX IS ORDERING, NOT CODE, and that is not a concession. After the cp NO gate can be green: the drift is real, `check_manifest` is right to fail, and make is right to stop. There is no driver change that makes step 0's gate meaningful — the only moment the precondition can be established is before the copy. Reordering the owner's own commands is therefore the correct and complete fix, and it costs nothing. . NOT CHANGED, deliberately: step 0 still offers the gate, and the offer is still worth taking. On a re-run after a builder fix, or any entry where the driver is already installed and custody re-signed, the gate runs in full and means what it says. Removing the offer would trade a sometimes-vacuous check for no check. | accepted | — | governance-paths | file: `docs/SITTING.md`; file: `docs/proposals/2026-08-31-m2-boundary-sitting/README.md`; file: `Makefile` |
| D0152 | A | Everything the M2 sitting's machinery got wrong, and why every fix is the owner's | The M2 boundary sitting completed on 2026-09-03 and exposed six defects in the machinery that ran it. The title does not count them because the count kept moving while this record was being written; item 6 is the one that matters most and was found last, by reading the gate's own passing output. None is fixed here, and that is not caution: every target is custody-set or author-key territory. `governance/tier-c.yaml`'s `custody.set` (:108-136) carries `.github/workflows/ci.yml` at :117, `scripts/custodian.sh` at :125, `scripts/boundary_sitting.sh` at :135 and `tests/poison/**/*` at :136; `ci.yml` and the fixture files additionally carry `MANIFEST.sha256` rows. Editing any of them breaks the owner's signature over `governance/custody.sha256`, so each fix is a Tier-C door the builder may not open. They are recorded and queued to the M3 boundary sitting, which is what the queue is for — no Tier-C request halts work (BRIEF §9.2). A sixth, in the same file as item 3, is recorded in D0153 because it is the collision's fingerprint rather than a defect the sitting's design invited. . ITEM 1 — THE D0141 RETARGET GUARD GREPS FOR A STRING ITS OWN REPLACEMENT WRITES. `boundary_sitting.sh:1461-1462` fires when `tests/poison/oracle-shadow-model/` exists AND `decisions/0141-*.yaml` still matches `fixture-candidates/oracle-shadow-model`. The replacement text the step writes contains the sentence "retargeted from docs/redteam/fixture-candidates/oracle-shadow-model/ by that same step" — so the guard's own success re-arms it, and it fires on a FINISHED sitting. Answering `y` then re-runs the replacement, whose `src.count(old) != 1` assertion cannot hold against already-retargeted bytes, and `die` stops the run. This is where both concurrent runs stopped. . The correct answer on a resumed sitting is `n`, and the `else` branch actively argues against it: "the check below will stop the sitting on this binding, and the message it prints tells you the retarget to make." That warning is written for a FRESH sitting, where the binding really is unresolved. On a resumed one the binding already resolves — `check_decisions` reported `0 unenforced` throughout — so declining is correct and nothing downstream stops. The fix is to test the POST-state (does the record name the installed path?) rather than the pre-state, which is the shape the step's own neighbours use. . AND THE TRIGGER PHRASE IS DELIBERATELY LEFT IN PLACE. D0141's binding detail is builder-landable, so rewording "retargeted from docs/redteam/fixture-candidates/…" would disarm this guard today at no cost. It is not reworded, for two reasons: the sentence is true and is the only surviving record of where that fixture came from, and removing it would falsify this record's own evidence while leaving the defect exactly where it is. A workaround that makes the bug unreproducible is worse than the bug. . ITEM 2 — STEP 4f'S SKIP-GUARD TESTS ONE OF THE THREE FILES ITS DECLINE BRANCH REVERTS. The guard is `boundary_sitting.sh:694`, `grep -q 'scripts/check_laws.py' Makefile`. The decline branch is `:786`, `git checkout -- Makefile .github/workflows/ci.yml tests/test_law_validation.py`. The set the guard reads is a strict subset of the set the revert writes, so any state where the Makefile is edited and the other two are not reads as "already in the Makefile — skipped" and the step never runs again. That state is reachable, and was reached (D0153): `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is today byte-identical to `docs/proposals/2026-08-25-boundary-sitting/ci.yml`, so step 4b's `diff -q` guard skips it too and no gate anywhere can see the gap. . What was actually lost is a comment. `ci.yml`'s whole job is `- run: make verify`, and the file has never executed — the repo has no remote, as its own header says. The effect is cosmetic; the shape is not. A guard that reads a subset of what it writes is the same class this project has now filed four times (D0071, D0091, D0149, and item 1 above): a check whose answer cannot depend on what it claims to check. . ITEM 3 — `custodian.sh:283-284` SIGNS THE ATTENTION RECEIPT WITHOUT CHECKING THE EXIT STATUS, and `:285` then prints "attention receipt written and author-signed" regardless. A failed `ssh-keygen -Y sign` — a locked agent, a missing key file, a declined touch on the hardware-backed owner key — produces a receipt with no `.sig` and a success line saying otherwise. The next `make verify` would catch it at `check_receipts` ("latest receipt is unsigned"), so this is not silent for ever; it is silent at the one moment the owner is standing there able to retry, and it fails in the direction of appearing to have worked. The receipt is the sole artifact the Tier-B silence-as-consent clock rests on (`_gov.py` `receipt_state`), which is why this is filed rather than shrugged at. Queue it beside D0146 item 2's missing `__pycache__` exclusion — same file, same sitting. . ITEM 4 — THE DRIVER HAS NO LOCK. The sitting is a single-run ceremony by construction and nothing in the driver says so. Two concurrent runs against one worktree produced item 2 and a duplicate attention receipt (D0153). A `flock` on a lockfile beside the transcript, refusing to start while another run holds it, is a few lines and removes the entire class. . ITEM 5 — THE INSTALLED FIXTURE'S OWN README STILL DESCRIBES IT AS STAGED AND UNPATCHED. `tests/poison/oracle-shadow-model/README.md` opens "**needs patch** — … Against the shipped check this fixture does not bite, which is why it is staged here and not in `tests/poison/`", and its reproduction command still names `PYTHONPATH=docs/redteam/fixture-candidates/oracle-shadow-model`, a path the sitting's own `git mv` deleted. Every clause is now false: D0142 replaced the two hardcoded name constants with `_frozen_oracles()`, which derives the map from `tests/laws/m*/_*.py` off the filesystem, and the fixture bites (see D0141's upgraded binding). The file is custody set, so the correction is the owner's; the staging-side copy at `docs/redteam/fixture-candidates/README.md`, which is neither frozen nor custody, is corrected by the builder in the same change as this record. . ITEM 6 — THE CUSTODIAN NEVER RUNS THE FIXTURE THIS SITTING INSTALLED, AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL. `tests/poison/oracle-shadow-model/` closes RT-M2-01, the M1->M2 pass's single CRITICAL finding. The sitting `git mv`d it into the sealed corpus, wrote its three `MANIFEST.sha256` rows, wrote its three `governance/custody.sha256` rows, and added its row to `tests/poison/README.md`'s table. It did NOT add the fourth thing the corpus's own installation recipe requires — a `poison` line in `scripts/custodian.sh`. Verified from the gate's passing output: the custodian prints sixteen "fails its poison as required" lines and none names oracle-shadow-model; `grep -c oracle-shadow-model scripts/custodian.sh` is 0. All thirteen other installed fixtures have their line. This one is the only gap. . WHY IT HAPPENED, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. Step 6 installs the custodian by comparing the live file against `$PROPOSALS_M1/custodian.sh` — the PREVIOUS milestone's draft — and its comment (`boundary_sitting.sh:1591-1592`) still reads "This sitting's own draft is the LIVE custodian.sh plus one new poison line for oracle-shadow (RT-M1-01)". That sentence was true at M1 and was carried into the M2 driver unchanged. `docs/proposals/2026-08-31-m2-boundary-sitting/` contains no `custodian.sh` at all, so there was no M2 draft to install: the comparison found the M1 draft already applied, printed "already applied — skipped", and the sitting proceeded. Nothing was declined and nothing failed; the step simply had nothing to offer. . THIS IS D0095'S SHAPE EXACTLY, ONE FILE OVER. `required_tags` lags because the session that mints a boundary tag may not edit the frozen file naming it required; the poison list lags because the sitting that installs a fixture installs a custodian drafted before that fixture existed. Both are hand-kept enumerations extended only at the moment their extender is least able to edit them. D0095's half (2) — "replace the enumeration with a rule that derives the required set" — is the fix both need, and the guard this sitting shipped shows it is achievable: D0142 replaced the oracle map's two hardcoded names with `_frozen_oracles()`, which reads `tests/laws/m*/_*.py` off the filesystem. A `poison` loop over `tests/poison/*/` that REFUSES a directory with no invocation would close this one the same way, and would have failed loudly on 2026-09-03 instead of finishing sooner. . WHAT IS AND IS NOT EXPOSED. The fixture is not unexercised: this change adds `tests/test_governance_scripts.py::test_oracle_shadow_model_fails_its_poison`, which runs it, and D0141's binding now points at that test. But `tests/test_governance_scripts.py` is neither frozen nor custody-set, so a builder may delete it and `custodian.sh` will still print "custody floor intact". The custody floor is the thing meant to hold when the builder is the adversary, and for this one fixture it currently does not. That is why this is item 6 and not a footnote to item 5. | accepted | — | governance-paths | file: `scripts/boundary_sitting.sh`; manifest: `scripts/custodian.sh`; manifest: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; manifest: `tests/poison/oracle-shadow-model/README.md`; pytest: `tests/test_governance_scripts.py::test_every_installed_fixture_is_exercised_by_this_suite` |
| D0153 | A | Two runs of a one-run ceremony, and an evidence root outside .gitignore | How the M2 boundary sitting was actually run, recorded because the transcript is not a record and this is the only place it will survive. The sitting closed correctly — `m2-close` verifies as owner@tannen over `25523a4`, closing commit `f089756`, tree clean — but it took three attempts, two of them concurrent, and the recovery method is worth more than the incident. . WHAT HAPPENED. Two invocations of `scripts/boundary_sitting.sh m2` were running against the same worktree at the same time, by accident. Both stopped at the same place — the D0141 retarget guard, D0152 item 1 — and both were killed by hand. The third run completed. . ARTIFACT 1 — A REVERTED FILE NO GATE CAN SEE. One run applied step 4f's edit to `Makefile`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `tests/test_law_validation.py`; the other was already past step 4f's guard, took a decline, and ran `git checkout --` over all three. Two were re-applied by the run that owned them; `ci.yml` was not, because the guard reads only the Makefile and now says "already — skipped". The lost bytes are a comment. The mechanism is D0152 item 2. . ARTIFACT 2 — TWO RECEIPTS AT ONE HEAD, AND A CHAIN LINE THAT VANISHED. `receipts/2026-09-02.md` and `receipts/2026-09-03.md` both record `HEAD: 14647976e9b447775f10049614898b764158d8ee`. Both are owner-signed and `check_receipts` accepts the pair, correctly: it requires each receipt's HEAD to be an ancestor of the next, and a commit is its own ancestor. The custodian overwrites `receipts/$(date +%F).md` unconditionally, so a re-run on a new day simply adds one. . The interesting half is what the second one is MISSING. `2026-09-02.md` carries "- previous receipt: 2026-08-31 at 64e0b155…"; `2026-09-03.md` carries no such line at all. `custodian.sh:268` computes `prev=$(ls -1 receipts/*.md | sort | tail -1)` and `:273` emits the line only `if [ "$prev" != "$receipt" ]`. The first run had already written `receipts/2026-09-03.md`, so the second run's `tail -1` returned the very file it was about to overwrite, the condition went false, and the chain line was dropped. THIS IS NOT COLLISION-SPECIFIC: any second custodian run on the same day loses that line, and `check_receipts` parses only `- HEAD:` so nothing anywhere notices. Filed as a sixth item against `custodian.sh` — author-key territory, so it queues to the M3 sitting beside D0152 item 3 and D0146 item 2, all three in the same file. . ARTIFACT 3 — AN EVIDENCE ROOT OUTSIDE `.gitignore`, WHICH WAS MINE. A hand pytest run during the assessment used `TANNEN_EVIDENCE_ROOT=.tannen-verify-evidence` — an invented name. `.gitignore:23` covers `.verify-evidence/` and nothing else, and step 9's `commit_with_hook_retry` does `git add -A`, so thirty-six evidence records rode into the sitting commit. Caught before any tag attested it, and removed at step 10's signing prompt — a moment when the driver is provably idle, blocked on `read` — with `git rm -r --cached` followed by `git commit --amend --no-verify`. Safe for four reasons, each checked rather than assumed: step 10 reads its DELEGATIONS and custody hashes from the WORKING TREE, which the amend does not touch; `git tag -s` resolves HEAD at signing time, after the amend; the attention receipt's recorded HEAD stayed an ancestor of the new commit; and no tag yet attested the old one. `git ls-tree -r HEAD` now returns zero such paths. . The `.gitignore` stanza above that line already argues this exact hazard — "a red gate leaves it behind, and the boundary sitting commits with `git add -A`". It names one path where the hazard is the pattern. The builder-side rule that follows: when running the suite by hand in this repo, use `.verify-evidence`, never an invented root. | accepted | — | governance-paths | file: `.gitignore`; manifest: `scripts/custodian.sh`; file: `scripts/check_receipts.py` |

Installing it is the sitting's owner-signed act; the draft existing is what makes step 6 reachable at all. . (2) D0152 ITEMS 1-5, IN ITS OWN NUMBERING. The D0141 retarget guard that re-arms on its own success and stops a resumed sitting (`boundary_sitting.sh:1461-1462`); step 4f's skip-guard reading one of the three files its decline branch reverts (`:694` vs `:786`); the receipt signed without checking `ssh-keygen -Y sign`'s exit status, with a success line printed regardless (`custodian.sh:283-285`); the driver having no lock though the sitting is a single-run ceremony (two concurrent runs produced D0153); and the installed fixture's README still opening "**needs patch**" while naming a reproduction path the sitting's own `git mv` deleted. . (3) D0153 — `custodian.sh:268` PICKS THE PREVIOUS RECEIPT WITH `tail -1`, AND `:273` DROPS THE CHAIN LINE ON ANY SAME-DAY RE-RUN, silently, because `$prev` then equals the receipt being written; `check_receipts` parses only `- HEAD:` so no guard notices a missing `previous receipt` line. Same file as item (2)'s third clause, same sitting. . (4) D0146 ITEM 2 — `custodian.sh:66` AND `check_manifest.py:113` DISAGREE ABOUT `__pycache__`. A `.pyc` written under `tests/poison/` leaves check_manifest green and the custodian red at `make verify`'s LAST step, ~37 minutes in, with a message ("not manifested") that invites the wrong fix. The one-line `find` exclusion is owner territory because the custodian is. . (5) D0148 ITEM 5 — A DECLINED SITTING IS NOT A NO-OP. The custodian writes and signs the receipt before the owner is asked to commit anything, so abandoning a decline leaves a signed receipt untracked, which step 0 clause (b) reads as sitting artifacts: the NEXT run starts `RESUMED=1` and skips the precondition gate. Moving the receipt behind a confirm reorders the receipt-then-tag argument (D0071), which is exactly why it needs the owner and a sitting rather than a quick edit. . (6) `governance/tag-roles.yaml` `required_tags` LAGS FOR THE THIRD TIME (D0095, then D0131 item 5, now here): `m3-laws-freeze` is minted this session under delegation 1 and cannot be added to the enumeration at :46-53 by the builder. The recurring shape — an enumeration extended only at the moment its extender may not edit it — is D0095 half (2)'s argument for deriving the set; until that lands, the row must be added at every boundary by hand. . (7) `scripts/check_laws.py` HAS NO POISON FIXTURE. The M2 sitting added it to the custody set (D0131 items 3-4, applied at step 4e), which makes it a guard the owner signs for — and it is the only custody-set guard with no fixture under `tests/poison/` and no `poison` line in the custodian, so BRIEF §9.1's guard-liveness-by-poison discipline does not cover the guard that can retire a frozen law. Verified this session: `grep check_laws scripts/custodian.sh` is empty and no `tests/poison/*` directory targets it. A fixture (e.g. a supersession entry whose successor does not exist, which check_laws must refuse) is a `tests/poison/` install — author-key territory twice over. . (8) D0143'S `event()` FOLLOW-UP, THE D0117 RESIDUE. D0130's `event()` counts are the quantity D0117 asks evidence records to carry, and they are reachable — but hypothesis writes its own retry bookkeeping into the same undifferentiated dict, so wiring them in today records a wall of version-dependent internals beside the law's declared shapes. (9) COSMETIC, FOR WHOEVER PREPARES THE M3 DRIVER: the M2 driver's transcript lines hardcode "712 tests" where the suite now runs 717; a re-run or a copied M3 driver inherits the stale count. Recorded so the M3 drafting session greps for it rather than rediscovering it. | accepted | — | governance-paths | file: `scripts/custodian.sh`; file: `scripts/boundary_sitting.sh`; file: `governance/tag-roles.yaml`; file: `docs/proposals/2026-09-04-m3-boundary-sitting/custodian.sh` |

| D0156 | A | A delta is a Rel over the same semiring — no Delta type — and delta-capability is declared per component, with B refused by name | A delta is a `Rel` over the same semiring as the relation it changes (docs/specs/m3.md §3.1). There is NO `Delta[K, S]` wrapper type. `Rel` already constructs negative ℤ counts — nothing in it inspects sign — the `rel/1` canonical form already encodes them, and the witnessed-row invariant (frozen L2.2/D0110) already does the right thing unprompted: `(-1, {{r}})` is accepted, `(-1, ∅)` refused. A retraction therefore owes provenance exactly as an arrival does, by a rule that already exists. . Delta-capability is DECLARED per component. A semiring is delta-capable when every component of its (possibly product) structure is either a GROUP component declaring `negate` with `add(a, negate(a)) == zero` law-checked where the other axioms are, or a `Why` component, for which `negate(w) = w` — `Why` is a join-semilattice under `add`, idempotent, no inverse. `Z` and `Z*Why` qualify; `B` declares no `negate` and every delta operation refuses it BY NAME. No M1 refusal lifts: `Z.multiplicity`/`collapse` still raise on a negative (§3.4 re-commissions those raises, D0158), so frozen L1.2 stays true by design. . REJECTED: a distinct `Delta[K, S]` type. It would double the operator surface — every bilinear rule would need `Rel × Δ`, `Δ × Rel` and `Δ × Δ` signatures — fork the store format, and contradict P4's one-annotated-relation-type principle. DBSP itself draws no such distinction: a delta is an element of the same abelian group as the state. The witnessed-row invariant already giving a retraction a provenance obligation is the tell that `Rel` was the right carrier all along. . REJECTED: guessing symmetric difference for `B` so it too could be delta-capable. A set semiring has no retractions; inventing one would be the silent coercion the door forbids (exactness-and-the-door). Refusing by name is the door working. | accepted | — | — | manifest: `docs/specs/m3.md`; manifest: `tests/laws/m3/test_l3_delta.py` |
| D0157 | A | apply's normalisation order is add → cone → group-zero drop → valuation, and byte identity is the L2–L4 equality — earned, not quotiented | `apply(base, delta, dead)` is pointwise addition followed by three normalisation steps IN THIS ORDER (docs/specs/m3.md §3.3): (1) the CONE CHECK — a row driven below the non-negative cone is an over-retraction, refused by name, which is where m1 §4.4's promised loud break lands, at the operation whose arguments made the question askable; (2) the GROUP-ZERO DROP — a row zero in every group component is dropped, `(0, {{r}})` included, because the reference has no such row; (3) the VALUATION — every surviving row's every `Why` is filtered by `surviving(w, dead)` (M2 §4, now kernel code). The criterion for step 2 is the group components, NOT the bag image: a positive count whose `Why` is empty must fall through to be refused by the witnessed-row invariant, never be dropped as bag-empty. Construction is untouched — a caller-built `(0, {{r}})` is still retained (frozen L1.4/D0093); `apply` is a new operation choosing what to EMIT. . L2, L3 and L4 assert CONTENT-ADDRESS equality — the same byte identity L1 gave replay and the golden corpus pins — not a quotient. For pure arrivals it is free: a `srcrow/1` ref depends on `(source, row)` only, so any partition unions identical refs idempotently while counts add commutatively. For retractions it is EARNED by step 3: `Why` is PosBool with no subtraction, so pointwise addition leaves the cumulative run's witnesses where the reference has the net run's, and `surviving(w, dead)` recovers the reference exactly on the positive fragment (the residue theorem, L3.11). `anti_join` sits outside that fragment and earns byte identity by replay instead (D0163's contagion rule). . REJECTED: equality up to bag image (a quotient). It states less than is true and silently abandons BRIEF §5.5's promise that the default pipeline's provenance survives a delta — L2.3 would become meaningless for any integral that ever saw a retraction. REJECTED: one-sided witness containment ("incremental ⊇ reference"). A semilattice cannot subtract, so apply-maintenance through `anti_join` is unsound; replaying is the honest rule, priced by BRIEF §10. The unsound variant is kept as the mutant `antijoin-delta-maintained`, and the `right-moves` perturbation stream draws the superseding-address case on purpose (D0118's rule paying for itself a second time). | D0167 | A | The delta executor's surface: code referenced by name, replay as a declared parameter, and the two trace properties advance INHERITS from M1 rather than invents | `tannen.incremental` is implemented at Session B against the surface frozen L3.15 pins (`DeltaNode`, `Ledger`/`Ledger.EMPTY`, `advance(...) -> .state_ref/.delta_ref/ .ledger_ref/.step_id/.rebuilt`). Five choices the spec left open, and two properties that need saying out loud because a reader will otherwise read them as bugs. . (1) CODE IS REFERENCED BY NAME. A `DeltaNode`'s descriptor is the content address of its declared form, and a lambda has no content address — a descriptor over one would be a lie. So `select` declares `predicate_id`, `map_rows` declares `map_id`, and `aggregate` declares `monoid_id` XOR `group_id`, each resolved out of a module-level registry (`PREDICATES`, `MAPS`, `MONOIDS`, `GROUPS`) with `register_*` for callers. The shipped registries are SEEDED with the M3 catalogue (`x-positive`, `k-only`, `sum`) because the frozen law files name those ids and the shipped package must resolve them. Re-registering a name with a different object is refused: a name a descriptor carries may not change meaning. Parameters are validated and the code they name resolved AT DECLARATION, not at the tick — a plan's mistakes should not wait for data to arrive to be found. . (2) `replay` IS A DECLARED PARAMETER, hence part of the descriptor. §4's contagion rule is a property of the caller's PLAN ("no `anti_join` at or below this node"), and the executor has no graph to compute it from (§7 declined one). So the caller declares it, and `distinct`/`aggregate`/`anti_join` replay whatever the caller says, because their rule is replacement regardless. . (3) FOUR VALUE TAGS: `deltaop/1` (the declared node), `incstate/1` (the node's integral refs — output always, inputs where the rule needs them: a `join` keeps both children's, a subtractive `aggregate` keeps its input's), `incstep/1` (what one step produced) and `ledger/1` (§6, spec-given). A column-set parameter is SORTED into the declared form, so two spellings of the same node are the same descriptor. . (4) THE TRACE IS CONSULTED, AND BY DEFAULT NOT WRITTEN; `record=True` is the caller's act. This is forced, and the force is worth recording: frozen `test_l3_15_a_tampered_trace_raises` calls `traces.record(done.step_id, <garbage>)` AFTER a successful `advance` and outside its `pytest.raises` block. `TraceStore.record` raises on a conflicting re-record, so if `advance` had recorded under `step_id` that line would raise and the frozen law would error rather than pass. The honest reading is that recording is a policy, exactly as M1 already makes it one between `AlwaysRebuild` and `VerifyingTrace`; `advance` takes the same choice as a flag, defaulting off. Consequently `rebuilt` reports whether this step's output was NEW TO THE STORE, not whether a function was called: everything a step produces is content-addressed, so a replay writes nothing and reports `rebuilt=False` whether or not a trace entry served it. §7's "replaying a stream hits traces" is therefore available (`record=True`) rather than automatic, which is a narrowing of the spec's prose and is queued for the M3 boundary sitting (D0154) as such. . (5) A NODE-LEVEL QUARANTINE IS UNREACHABLE FROM `advance`, and the guard stays. Its inputs are relations loaded from the store, never an upstream `Quarantine`, so only ROW-level quarantine can arise; those rows are stored and named by `quarantined_ref` — reports about a tick, never state (BRIEF P3) — and the integral simply lacks them. `Advanced.quarantine` is the P3 rule stated where it belongs, not a path this suite reaches. . INHERITED, NOT INVENTED: `step_id` is `derivation_id(descriptor, inputs)`, which m1 §8 defines as ORDER-INSENSITIVE in the inputs, and §7 pins that formula ("sorted delta refs"). So a binary node's operand order is not part of its step id, and `advance(node, None, [a, b])` and `advance(node, None, [b, a])` share a step id while computing different things. This is M1's own property — `Node(transform, inputs)` has it identically, since `f(a, b)` and `f(b, a)` share a derivation id there too — carried forward rather than quietly diverged from. It is pinned by a test that says so, it is the second reason `advance` does not record by default, and it is queued for the sitting alongside (4). | accepted | — | public-surface | file: `src/tannen/incremental.py`; manifest: `tests/laws/m3/test_l3_executor.py`; pytest: `tests/test_incremental.py::test_a_replayed_step_is_served_from_the_trace_when_the_caller_records`; pytest: `tests/test_incremental.py::test_a_binary_step_id_inherits_derivation_ids_order_insensitivity`; pytest: `tests/test_incremental.py::test_a_node_is_refused_at_declaration_not_at_the_tick`; pytest: `tests/test_incremental.py::test_the_contagion_rule_sheds_a_superseded_anti_join_address` |

(1) `kernel.delta.group_slots(S)` is `why_slots`' counterpart: every location that can SUBTRACT, by the same recursive descent, in the same path vocabulary. This record is not a second authorisation. It is the execution, the two things the execution turns out to cost that D0115 did not price, and the one question D0115 never asked. . OWNER RULINGS TAKEN 2026-09-06, in conversation, and queued here for signature the way D0115 itself was: (1) excise all 12 sibling snapshot files from history, not merely from the published tree; (2) licence the result Apache-2.0, superseding the MIT/CC-BY-SA-4.0 split in `policy.yaml licence_defaults` — which that file already says is a default and not a publication decision. . === WHY MECHANISM (a) IS NOT A REDACTION, MEASURED === . D0115 recommends keeping the snapshots and excluding them from the published tree. `concepts/snapshots/**` entered at the ROOT COMMIT `5c3a474` and has been touched in exactly one commit in the repository's life, so all 594 lines sit in the tree of every one of the 77 commits across all five branches. Deleting them at HEAD leaves them one `git show 5c3a474` away. And the history is what gets published: `.github/workflows/ ci.yml` pins `fetch-depth: 0` because the receipt chain asserts ancestry between recorded HEADs and the tag set is part of the custody floor. Mechanism (a) is still needed — it is what lets the registry verify once the bytes are gone — but it is the CONSEQUENCE of an excision, never a substitute for one. . === WHAT THE REWRITE COSTS, REHEARSED RATHER THAN ASSERTED === . `docs/proposals/2026-09-06-publication/rehearse_rewrite.sh`, 14 steps, in a disposable clone; the source repository was never written to. 77 commits in, 77 out, none dropped, a complete 77-pair `commit-map` with zero null entries. The 12 files are absent from every commit of every ref; `concepts/snapshots/semiring-relations/` — this project's excerpt of its own BRIEF — survives, which keeps `check_concepts.py`'s byte-verifying path non-vacuous in the published tree rather than leaving it a branch nothing takes. . ALL EIGHT TAGS: `object CHANGED / signature BROKEN`, measured, every one. That includes `brief-freeze`, whose TAG OBJECT hash `c219e63819beb4052b326e47b9cbd5d208779cda` is pinned at `governance/tag-roles.yaml#trust_root.object` — the file that calls re-issuing it "the one act that would otherwise redefine every other check in the custody floor", and which `check_tag_signers.py` exists to detect. This plan performs that act deliberately, under signature, with the old value preserved here. Re-creation works: the four builder tags were re-signed with the real builder key at their ORIGINAL tagger dates via `GIT_COMMITTER_DATE` and all four verify with dates unchanged, so `bless_epoch` and D0036's delegation-precedes-signature ordering are undisturbed. . === THE RECEIPTS ARE NOT RE-SIGNED, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN === . A rewrite kills all five: `check_receipts.py` runs `cat-file -e` on each recorded HEAD and every one becomes a non-commit. The obvious repair — edit each receipt to carry the new SHA and re-sign — fabricates an attestation of a moment nobody attested to, which is the precise thing the chain exists to prevent. Refused. . Instead the five receipts stay BYTE-IDENTICAL and the rewrite declares itself: `receipts/REWRITE-<date>.md`, owner-signed under its own namespace `tannen-rewrite` (distinct from `tannen-receipt` so neither signature can be replayed as the other), carrying the COMPLETE old->new map. `check_receipts.py` resolves each recorded HEAD through the map before looking it up. The chain then verifies end to end through a discontinuity that is itself signed, dated and public — which is strictly more than an un-rewritten history proves about itself. . Measured: against the rewritten history the shipped guard reports five "the history the owner attested to is gone" failures; with the patch and a signed attestation all five clear, with no receipt or receipt signature touched. Three negative controls, each watched going red per D0111/D0116 — attestation removed (the five failures return); attestation present but unsigned ("unsigned, it is the rewriting party vouching for itself"); attestation signed but map tampered (red twice, on the signature AND on the remapped commit being absent). And no regression: against the real un-rewritten tree the patched guard prints exactly what the shipped one prints. . === THE PIN COUNT, AND THE VACUITY IT CLOSES === . D0115 makes one condition non-optional: a degraded `check_concepts.py` must COUNT the pins it verified against an expectation not derived from the files it is checking, or publication installs species I of D0116's taxonomy inside its own publication door. The expectation goes in `governance/policy.yaml` (`concept_registry.expected_citation_pins: 13`) — owner-signed, in `required_signatures`, and not a file the degraded path also skips. Thirteen is measured: 13 `snapshot.path` entries across 8 records, all unique. Eight probes, all run: baseline 13-by-bytes green; one snapshot absent -> 12+1 green; the PUBLISHED configuration (all 12 gone) -> 1+12 green where the shipped guard reports 12 failures; then a concept record truncated away (11 != 13), the expectation key deleted, `policy.yaml` deleted outright, and `concepts/` emptied — all four RED. The shipped poison fixture still fails and still carries its marker. . === WHAT EXCISION DOES NOT REMOVE — THE QUESTION D0115 NEVER ASKED === . The plan this executes carried an acceptance test `git log --all -p -S 'renavon' -- concepts/` -> empty. The rehearsal falsified it, and the correction is the most useful thing this record carries. The borrowed TEXT goes; the CITATIONS stay, because they are what BRIEF §2 is for. A public reader still learns from `concepts/*.yaml`: four repository URLs including `renavondata/renavon-monorepo`; nine document paths including `docs/architecture/decisions/002-pipeline-rigour-stance.md`; section titles quoted verbatim, the renavon row's being an internal ADR heading; five pinned commit SHAs of private repositories. And `BRIEF.md` — frozen at `brief-freeze`, constitutional, unamendable — names all four in its §1 constellation table and describes the last as "The business; funds and supplies the empirical substrate". . So the owner's ruling answered "may this repo quote 58 lines of that ADR" and the remaining question is "may this repo NAME that repository, its ADR path and its section heading in public". They are different questions and only the first was put. If the answer to the second is also no, the renavon `source` entry leaves `concepts/provenance-ref-grammar.yaml`, `expected_citation_pins` becomes 12, the concept keeps its pkm source and stays `S-pending`, and the registry loses one of the two owners BRIEF §2 names for that row — a weakening of the citation discipline, not a tidy-up. It is queued as part of this record rather than guessed at. . === ALSO CORRECTED HERE, BECAUSE D0045 MAKES D0115 IMMUTABLE === . D0115 binds `governance/policy.yaml#external_surface.publishing` with `strength: enforced`. Measured at `5f206cc`: that key is read by NOTHING. It appears in prose and in the `check-manifest-unsigned-policy` poison fixture, nowhere in any guard. Its owner signature makes the clause unforgeable; no guard consults it before bytes leave. The binding should read `documentary`. And per D0175 the home-path disclosure count D0115 shows the owner is five, not four. . === STAGED, NOT APPLIED === . Nothing in `docs/proposals/2026-09-06-publication/` is applied: two patches to custody-set guards, three owner edits to signed files, four root files (a LICENSE at the root IS the grant, which is why D0115 refused to pre-write one and why this record does not either), and one poison fixture candidate. | D0177 | A | scripts/custodian.sh prints 'attention receipt written and author-signed' when ssh-keygen failed — an unsigned receipt left in the store, a false success line, exit 0, and the only context it fires in is a sitting | Found by running `scripts/custodian.sh` bare as the `m3 -> master` merge gate, on a machine that does not hold the owner key's passphrase. Reported, not fixed: the file is author-key territory (BRIEF §9.1, CLAUDE.md hard rules). The patch is drafted at `docs/proposals/2026-09-06-publication/patches/04-custodian-receipt-signing.md` for the sitting that is already being assembled. . `scripts/custodian.sh:283-285` runs `ssh-keygen -Y sign` and never reads its exit status, then unconditionally says so. Observed verbatim: . "custodian: custody floor intact / Enter passphrase for ".../tannen_owner": Load key ".../tannen_owner": incorrect passphrase supplied to decrypt private key / custodian: attention receipt written and author-signed: receipts/2026-09-06.md (+ .sig)" . There is no `.sig`. The custodian exited 0 having written an UNSIGNED receipt into `receipts/`, asserted it was signed, named a file that does not exist, and reported the custody floor intact. . WHY IT IS WORSE THAN A COSMETIC MESSAGE. The receipt step runs AFTER `check_receipts.py` and only when the custodian is invoked bare — `make verify` passes `--check-only` and skips it. So the single context in which this fires is a boundary sitting, which is the worst available one: the step appears to succeed and the damage surfaces on the NEXT custodian run, by which time the operator has moved on. It is also the artifact that starts the Tier-B silence-as-consent clock, so an unsigned receipt between two runs is a clock nobody can verify started. . IT DOES SELF-DETECT, WHICH BOUNDS IT, AND THE CONTROL WAS RUN RATHER THAN ASSUMED: `check_receipts: FAIL (1 violation(s)) — receipts/2026-09-06.md has no signature. A receipt is an attestation of presence; an unsigned one attests to nothing...`. That is the guard working. But "the next run catches it" is not the property line 285 claims, and a custody floor whose last line can be false is exactly the class this repository spends its effort on — D0116's taxonomy, and the same shape as D0112's credential filter that could not fail. . THE FIX IS FOUR LINES: test the exit status; on failure `rm -f` the receipt this step created three lines earlier and call `bad`, which already increments FAIL so the custodian exits non-zero. The deletion is the only one in the script and touches nothing that was ever signed, committed or attested — an unsigned receipt is worse than no receipt, because it reddens every later run for a file that should never have been left behind. . HOUSEKEEPING, STATED SO IT IS NOT DISCOVERED LATER. The unsigned `receipts/2026-09-06.md` was untracked, was never committed, was removed within minutes, and `check_receipts.py` was re-run to confirm `5 receipt(s); chain unbroken to HEAD`. A copy is held outside the repository as evidence for the drafted patch. The receipt chain is byte-for-byte what it was before the run. . AND A SECOND, SMALLER LESSON: running the custodian bare has a WRITE side effect on `receipts/`, which is owner-attestation territory. Nothing warns about that at the call site. A builder session's default invocation should be `--check-only`; this one was not, which is how the defect was found, and is the reason it is worth writing down rather than filing as bad luck. | accepted | — | governance-paths | file: `docs/proposals/2026-09-06-publication/patches/04-custodian-receipt-signing.md`; pytest: `tests/test_governance_scripts.py::test_check_passes_on_real_tree`; manifest: `scripts/custodian.sh` |

It had teeth: the pattern was `-- Step` and the driver prints `== Step`, grep matched nothing, and because `LAST_STEP=$(last_step)` is an assignment-only statement, under `set -euo pipefail` the failing substitution became the statement's status and KILLED THE HARNESS MID-VERDICT — not one loud check but no verdict at all. MEASURED with a throwaway passphrase-protected ed25519 key, three invocations, the driver's exact shape (`ssh-keygen -Y sign -f "$OWNER_KEY" -n <namespace> <file>`): . (b) `-f <PUBLIC KEY>` with ssh-agent holding the private half: signs silently, and the signature verifies against `allowed_signers`. . (c) `-f <PRIVATE KEY PATH>` with ssh-agent holding it: ALSO SIGNS SILENTLY, rc 0. This is the one that matters. ssh-keygen finds the key in the agent and never asks, with `-f` still pointing at the private path exactly as the driver already writes it. **So the fix needs no code: one `ssh-add` before the sitting makes all fourteen key touches silent.** . Measured against the real keys, WITHOUT signing anything with them — `ssh-keygen -y -P ''` fails fast on an encrypted key and `ssh-keygen -lf` reads the public half out of the private file without decrypting it, so neither probe prompts: `~/.ssh/tannen_owner` IS passphrase-protected and was not in any agent; `~/.ssh/tannen_builder` is not, which is what `DELEGATIONS.md` intends for an unattended builder key. As things stood, the sitting would have prompted ten times. . The report runs in `--dry-run` too, under its own header before the precondition: the probes never sign, never prompt and never read a passphrase, and a preview of the sitting is exactly where an owner wants to be told they are about to be asked for a passphrase ten times. Guarding it on `$DRY` was the first spelling and was wrong for that reason. . These are SSH signatures, so the machinery is ssh-agent. Not gpg-agent, no pinentry, and no cache TTL to expire — but `ssh-add -t` would introduce one, so the report says not to use it: the sitting runs about 95 minutes. . The driver clones `$PWD`, which is a WORKTREE, so the clone carries only that worktree's branch; and `git filter-repo` DROPS the remote-tracking refs rather than converting them to local branches. Measured on the rewritten clone: `refs/heads/m3` and the eight tags, no `master`, no remotes. This would have surfaced at the LAST step of the sitting: after ninety-five minutes, after all fourteen signatures, with `gh repo create` already run. Nothing in the repository was at risk — but the sitting's final act would have been improvised. . THE DEFECT INTRODUCED WHILE FIXING IT, which is the more useful half of this record. The first spelling put the create/checkout/delete logic INSIDE `ff_master`. `ff_master` is called three times: on `$WORK` twice, and at step 5 on `.` — the owner's real repository, to bring `master` up to date before the clone is taken. On the real repository, where `master` DOES exist, that spelling would have switched the m3 worktree to `master` and then run `git branch -D m3`, deleting the milestone branch from the live repo. . IT PASSED THE REHEARSAL, 52 of 52. Two reasons, both worth keeping: . (1) THE FIXTURE WAS SYSTEMATICALLY UNLIKE THE THING IT STOOD FOR. The harness clones a worktree, and a worktree clone has no `master`, so every run took the create-branch path where the deletion is harmless. The dangerous path — `master` exists — was unreachable by construction. The harness now creates `master` in its clone so the fixture exercises the path the owner will, and four checks assert the sitting leaves the repository on its own branch with that branch still existing, and leaves the clone with exactly one branch named `master`. Watched failing on a mutant driver that calls `publish_shape` on the repository, which is the hazard exactly. . MEASURED, after the split: the full mechanics-only run is 56 of 56 with no `fatal:` line in the transcript and the rewritten clone carrying one branch named `master`; the mutant that calls `publish_shape` on the repository is 54 ok and EXACTLY 2 FAIL — the two branch checks, and nothing else. An earlier spelling of that control reddened 25 checks in a cascade, which is evidence the hazard is real but poor evidence about what the checks measure; the isolated version is the useful one. . TWO SMALLER THINGS FIXED WHILE HERE. `publish_shape` would have checked out an existing `master` without confirming it was at HEAD — unreachable where the driver calls it, since a fresh clone has none, but it now fast-forwards a stale master and refuses one that is not an ancestor. And the harness's isolation control — "the real repo's working tree is untouched" — now PRINTS THE DIFFERENCE when it fails. It compares a snapshot taken before the driver ran with one taken after, so an edit made in another window during a three-hour run reads exactly like the driver writing into the real repository. That misreading happened here, cost a diagnosis, and is now answered by the check itself. . (2) THE FAILURE WAS SILENT UNDER `set -e`. `run git … branch -f master HEAD && note "…"` puts the failing command in an AND list, where errexit does not apply, so `fatal: cannot force update the branch 'master' used by worktree at …` scrolled past inside a green run. Only the harness's unexpected-failure-lines scan of the transcript surfaced it, and that scan fails no check — it prints. That is the right design for a scan that cannot know which lines matter, and it is also why a green verdict is never the whole reading of a run. | accepted | — | governance-paths, public-surface | file: `docs/proposals/2026-09-06-publication/publication_sitting.sh`; file: `docs/proposals/2026-09-06-publication/rehearse_publication.sh`; file: `docs/proposals/2026-09-06-publication/README.md` |
| D0187 | A | Adoption of the published history is a remap through the signed attestation, not a fetch and reset — and the working branch is the one branch that must NOT be remapped, which only running the guards on the result revealed | `docs/proposals/2026-09-06-publication/adopt_published_history.sh` points the LOCAL repository at the published, rewritten history, and `rehearse_adoption.sh` runs it against a disposable copy of that repository with a real, signed commit map. Neither is applied; the owner runs adoption after the push and after CI is green, and the script refuses without `--ci-green`, which is the owner asserting they looked. . WHY IT IS NOT `git fetch && git reset --hard origin/master`. The published repository carries ONE branch, `master`, and eight tags — no `m0`/`m1`/`m2`/`m3` refs at all (D0186). There is nothing to reset the milestone branches TO. Each must be resolved through the complete old->new commit map in `receipts/REWRITE-<date>.md`, which is what that owner-signed artifact exists for (D0176). The script verifies that signature under `tannen-rewrite` BEFORE it trusts a single pair, and stops on any branch whose tip is not in the map rather than guessing at one. . THE DEFECT THE REHEARSAL FOUND, and it is the whole reason this has a record rather than three lines in a README. The first version remapped EVERY branch, `master` included. Every ref-level check passed — 35 of them: branches moved, each new tip existed in the published history, every old tip resolved under the backup namespace, all four worktrees clean and on their branch's new tip, all eight tags replaced, nothing left in the incoming namespace, the real repository untouched. And the repository was still wrong. The sitting makes TWO commits of its own — the pre-rewrite commit A and the post-rewrite commit C — which exist only in the published history and have no pre-publication counterpart to map from. So remapping `master` lands it two commits BEFORE the publication: no attestation in the tree, an unpatched `check_receipts.py`, the old trust root still pinned in `tag-roles.yaml`, and the re-signed tags sitting beside all of it. `check_receipts`, `check_tag_signers` and the custodian all go red, from one cause, and the repository reads as broken when it is merely at the wrong commit. . TWO RULES, then. A HISTORICAL branch (m0, m1, m2) marks a point in the past and resolves through the map to the same point in the rewritten history. The WORKING branch — `master`, and any branch sitting on master's tip, which is how `m3` is arranged here — takes the PUBLISHED HEAD. Measured: 40 of 40, the three guards green on the adopted repository, and `m0 2c70d735 -> 7dea211b`, `m1 4845d9fb -> d4240734`, `m2 54c3da9b -> 49faf936` through the map while `m3` and `master` both take the published head. . "THE REFS MOVED CORRECTLY" AND "THE REPOSITORY WORKS" ARE DIFFERENT CLAIMS. That is the generalisable finding, and it is D0186's shape one level up: a verdict can be green across every check it has and still be measuring the wrong thing. The harness now runs `check_receipts`, `check_tag_signers` and the custodian on the adopted repository, and asserts that `master` is EXACTLY the published head rather than any remap of it. . The negative control makes the point exactly. A mutant that removes the two-rule distinction scores 35 ok and 5 FAIL — and THE 35 THAT PASS ARE THE SAME 35 REF-LEVEL CHECKS THAT PASSED BEFORE THE DEFECT WAS FOUND. The five that fail are the two new assertions about the published head and the attestation, and the three guards. The defect is invisible to every check that asks whether the refs moved correctly and visible only to the ones that ask whether the repository works. . WHAT IT NEVER DOES. Touch the stash — shared across worktrees, so entries made against the old history will apply to the new one only by luck; it reports them and stops there. Move anything before every pre-publication ref is copied under `refs/backup/pre-publication-<date>/`, so every SHA named in 186 decision records stays resolvable and the whole adoption is reversible. Or run while any worktree has uncommitted work: `git branch -f` REFUSES a branch checked out in a worktree, so the script moves those from inside the worktree with `reset --hard`, which would silently discard the work. | accepted | — | governance-paths | file: `docs/proposals/2026-09-06-publication/adopt_published_history.sh`; file: `docs/proposals/2026-09-06-publication/rehearse_adoption.sh`; file: `decisions/0186-the-rewritten-clone-had-no-master-branch-and-the-fix-would-have-deleted-the-owners.yaml` |
