| D0189 | A | The owner's rewrite clone came out of the sitting carrying four branches, because the one-branch fix deleted only the branch HEAD happened to be on — and the rehearsal could not see it, for the third time and the same reason | `publish_shape` deletes EVERY branch in the rewrite clone that is not `master`, not just the one that was checked out, using `git branch -d` and never `-D` — the refusal of an unmerged branch IS the merge proof, and an unexpected branch must stop the sitting rather than have its commits dropped silently. It records each deletion in a `shape` file beside the step breadcrumb. The owner's ruling, given on being shown the four: publish only `master`, with everything merged into it. . THE DEFECT, found at the owner's real sitting — the first one this package's rehearsals did not find first. D0186 established that the published clone carries one branch named `master`, and wrote `publish_shape` to make it so. That function creates `master`, checks it out, and deletes `$cur`, the branch HEAD arrived on. Measured on the sitting's actual output at `/var/tmp/tannen-rewrite.NzJIPj`: `m0 m1 m2 master`. It deleted `m3` and left three. . D0186's stated mechanism was half right and the half that was wrong is the interesting one. `git filter-repo` does not simply DROP remote-tracking refs — it converts `refs/remotes/ origin/*` into local branches. It dropped them in the harness because the harness clones a clone of a worktree, which carried only the branches the harness had put there. The owner's repository is a bare repo with five branches and four worktrees, so its clone carried five remote refs, and filter-repo made five local branches out of them. . NOTHING WAS PUBLISHED WRONG, because the guard written for exactly this refused: `publish: STOP — /var/tmp/tannen-rewrite.NzJIPj has 4 branches; the sitting leaves exactly one (D0186)`. D0188's push script checks the shape it is handed instead of trusting the driver that produced it, and that is the whole return on writing it. The sitting stopped one step from the push, with the irreversible middle already done and correct. . THE FIXTURE WAS UNLIKE THE THING IT STOOD FOR, AGAIN — the third instance, and D0186's own record is where the first two are written down. D0186 fixed the fixture by adding ONE branch, `master`, which made the create-branch path unreachable and the delete-one-branch path exercised. Two branches minus one deleted is one branch, so "the rewritten clone carries exactly one branch" passed — for a clone that had exactly one branch too many, never three. The check was right, the fixture could not make it fail, and the pass carried no information. That is the same shape as the two failures D0186 records, produced by the fix for them. . THE CHECK NOW HAS A POSITIVE CONTROL. The harness gives its clone two extra sibling branches, so the rewrite clone arrives with four and `publish_shape` must delete three; and a new check asserts the driver recorded at least two deletions. The driver STATES what it deleted, in a file, the way it already states which step it reached — the harness does not learn the driver's state by parsing the driver's prose. A one-branch clone now fails the control instead of passing the guarantee. . WHAT WAS DONE TO THE CLONE, and what it cost. `git branch -d m0 m1 m2` — all three accepted, which is git asserting they are merged into master; `git log --branches --not master` was empty before and after; all 91 commits and all 8 tags still reachable from `master`. One thing IS lost and is recorded rather than glossed: the branch tips sat 5, 2 and 2 commits AHEAD of their `m0-close`, `m1-close` and `m2-close` tags, so those three commits are no longer named by any ref. They remain in `master`'s history. No replacement tag was made: every tag must verify under `check_tag_signers` against the repinned trust root, and an unsigned marker tag would redden a guard to preserve a label. . HOW THE FIX WAS VERIFIED, AND WHY NOT BY THE REHEARSAL. The rehearsal can no longer run this sitting end to end against this repository, and finding that out is the other half of this record. Step 5b derives the scrub expressions by reading `concepts/provenance-ref-grammar.yaml` at PRE_HEAD and asserting exactly one source whose repo names renavon. The sitting has now HAPPENED: commit A removed that source and left `omits: [renavon]` in its place, so the assertion finds 0 and the driver stops — `publication: STOP — could not derive the scrub expressions`. The sitting is not idempotent past its own first commit, and a re-run would have to start from a tree that predates it (`3f8634b`), not from the tree as it stands. That was never stated anywhere, and the driver's abort text does not say it. . So the branch fix is verified at the level of the function instead, against the real bytes extracted from the driver rather than a re-implementation of them. Measured, all three: a synthetic clone shaped like the owner's (`m0 m1 m2 m3 master`) comes out of the fixed `publish_shape` as `master` alone, HEAD on master, with four lines in the shape file; the SAME fixture through the version committed at `3de45cc` comes out as `m0 m1 m2 master`, which is the owner's clone reproduced exactly and is the defect watched failing; and a clone carrying a branch with a commit master does not have stops the sitting — `DIE: branch 'stray' … is not merged into master — refusing to drop it` — with the branch still there afterwards. . The aborted rehearsal was not wasted, because the new control is what reported the abort's consequence: the run stopped before step 5c, so the rewrite clone never reached `publish_shape` and `the rewritten clone carries exactly one branch` PASSED — on a clone that had one branch because nothing had happened to it. `and publish_shape actually had siblings to delete` failed in the same run. That is the check catching a vacuous pass on the first occasion it could, which is the entire reason it exists. | accepted | — | governance-paths, public-surface | file: `docs/proposals/2026-09-06-publication/publication_sitting.sh`; file: `docs/proposals/2026-09-06-publication/rehearse_publication.sh`; file: `docs/proposals/2026-09-06-publication/publish_push.sh` |

D0187 established two rules — a historical branch resolves through the map, and `master` takes the published head, because the sitting's own commits A and C exist only in the published history and have no pre-publication counterpart to map from. D0189's commit landed on `master` the following morning — the fix for the branch shape, written while preparing this same publication — and from that moment "take the published head" meant "discard D0189". . Nothing would have been destroyed: the script backs every ref up under `refs/backup/pre-publication-<date>/` before it moves anything, and it says so. But `master` would have come out one commit short with nothing announcing it, and the record of why the published repository has one branch would have been the thing missing. A loss you have to notice yourself is the half of a data loss that guards are for. . | D0191 | A | CI's first-ever run failed because the repository advertises a Python floor it has never been able to meet, and only a machine that was not the builder's could see it | `.python-version` pins `3.13`, so every environment resolves the interpreter the frozen law suite was written against instead of whatever the host happens to offer. It is an unfrozen path, which is the only reason this fix is available to a builder at all. . THE DEFECT. `pyproject.toml` declares `requires-python = ">=3.12"`. The frozen M1 replay law cannot pass on 3.12. `tests/laws/m1/test_l1_replay.py` runs its fixture in fresh interpreters via `python -c "<source>"` — deliberately, so that hash-order dependence is reachable rather than theoretical — and the kernel hashes a transform's SOURCE TEXT before admitting it to a graph (BRIEF §5.1). On 3.12 `inspect.getsource` cannot recover source for code entered with `-c`, so `transform.register` raises `TransformError: 'pipeline': source text is unavailable`. On 3.13 the same call returns the source and all four nodes pass. Measured directly, both interpreters, one probe: 3.13.14 prints `SOURCE AVAILABLE`; 3.12.13 prints `NO SOURCE: could not get source code`. . HOW IT SURFACED, which is the part worth keeping. `make verify` has been green on this machine for every milestone, and this machine has 3.13.14. The GitHub runner resolved CPython 3.12.3 — Ubuntu's system interpreter, which satisfies `>=3.12` — and `check_decisions` reported two records whose pytest binding does not resolve (D0100, D0101, both binding the same file). Nothing else on the runner was red: `check_manifest` OK, `check_concepts` OK, the checkout with `fetch-depth: 0` correct. The claim ">=3.12" was never true and could not be falsified by any local run, because a local run never chose 3.12. This is precisely what publishing was for. . WHAT THIS FIX DOES NOT DO. It pins the toolchain; it does not correct the false claim. `pyproject.toml` is a FROZEN path (`MANIFEST.sha256`), so `requires-python` cannot be raised to `>=3.13` by a builder. Until it is, the package metadata still tells an installer that 3.12 will work, and it will not. **That correction is queued for the next boundary sitting, where frozen paths can change.** Recorded here rather than left implicit, because a pin that makes a red thing green while the untrue statement survives is exactly the shape of a fix that gets forgotten. . Note that `uv sync --frozen` on the runner must now DOWNLOAD 3.13 rather than use the system interpreter. That is uv's default behaviour for a `.python-version` it cannot satisfy locally, and the workflow is frozen, so it could not have been passed `-p 3.13` instead even if that were preferable. | accepted | — | public-surface | file: `.python-version` |
| D0192 | A | The replay recipe printed by yesterday's new guard could not have satisfied that guard, because a cherry-pick's new sha is no more in the map than the original was | The post-sitting-commit guard in `adopt_published_history.sh` now asks whether a commit is in the PUBLISHED HISTORY (`git rev-list master --not "$NEW_HEAD"`), not merely whether the rewrite map knows it. D0190 added a guard that refuses adoption when `master` carries a commit the published map does not know, and printed a recipe: cherry-pick the outstanding commits onto the published head, move `master`, re-run. That recipe cannot pass the guard it is printed by. The guard was correct about the hazard and wrong about the remedy, and would have read as a loop. . Asking about the published history instead is right for both states and not only for this one. Before publication the histories are disjoint, so `--not "$NEW_HEAD"` excludes nothing and every local commit is tested against the map: the two post-sitting commits are named, as they should be. After the replay is PUSHED, those commits are in the published history, the exclusion removes them, and the guard falls silent — because the thing it was worried about has actually been fixed rather than renamed. . Found by reasoning about the recipe while writing it out for the owner, not by running it — which is worth stating plainly, because everything else in this package was found by running something. | D0193 | A | The post-sitting guard had no answer for work replayed somewhere it cannot see, so the first real adoption went around it by hand; --accept-unmapped is that manoeuvre made checkable | `adopt_published_history.sh` takes a repeatable `--accept-unmapped <sha>`. The assertion is not taken on trust: the script re-derives that commit's own paths from its diff and looks each one up at the published head, refusing the flag if an added or modified path is missing there, if a deleted path is still present, or if not one path matches byte for byte. . THE GAP. D0190 refuses to adopt while `master` carries a commit the published history does not have; D0192 fixed its remedy to replay -> push -> adopt. Both assume the replay happens HERE. At the real adoption it had not: D0189's and D0190's fixes were made in the rewrite clone, mid-sitting, because that is where the sitting's own defects surface. Their content shipped; their local shas never will be in the map, and no number of re-runs changes that — there is nothing left to replay. The guard was right to refuse and had no exit, so the first real adoption was performed by hand: verify both records byte-identical at the published head, name the old tip under `refs/backup/pre-publication-2026-09-08/`, reset `master` to commit A, run the script. Measured against the two real commits it reports 2 identical + 2 changed downstream and 4 identical + 2 changed — the same numbers the manual check produced, now printed by the script instead of by a person. A commit whose file is genuinely absent is refused; so is a flag naming a commit that was mapped all along, which would otherwise read as cover for the commit actually at risk. . Verified by running all five states against a disposable bare clone fetching the real published repository: no flag still refuses and names both commits; the flag on a mapped sha refuses; the flag on a fabricated commit carrying a file that never shipped refuses naming that file (and again with a space in that path, since the report is what justifies accepting the flag and must not split one entry into two); the flag on a commit whose every path is byte-identical passes with nothing changed downstream; the flag on both real commits passes and adopts to the published head. | accepted | — | governance-paths | file: `docs/proposals/2026-09-06-publication/adopt_published_history.sh` |
| D0194 | A | The Python floor was the builder's to correct all along: D0191 read a poison fixture's own pyproject.toml as proof that the root one was frozen, and queued a twenty-second edit to a ceremony | CORRECTION TO D0191, filed as a new record because decision fields are immutable (D0045). D0191 states that `pyproject.toml` is a FROZEN path and concludes that raising `requires-python` "is queued for the next boundary sitting, where frozen paths can change." Both halves are false. The root `pyproject.toml` is neither frozen nor custody-set, and it is excluded from both ON PURPOSE. . MEASURED, four ways. `MANIFEST.sha256` contains exactly one row matching `pyproject`, and it is `tests/poison/lint-imports/pyproject.toml` (:19) — a poison fixture's own file, not this one. `governance/custody.sha256` contains the same single row (:67). `governance/tier-c.yaml` :103 says "pyproject.toml is deliberately NOT listed: dependency work would otherwise halt mid-milestone." `docs/SITTING.md`:111-113 says the same thing in the same words, and adds where the guarantee actually lives: "its import contracts are covered instead by the contract-shape check inside `check_manifest`." . SO THE FIX IS LANDED HERE, by a builder, in this record's own commit: `requires-python = ">=3.13"`, matching `.python-version` and the interpreter the frozen law suite is actually green on. `uv.lock` is regenerated with it — 1 insertion, 74 deletions, every deletion a cp312 or graalpy312 wheel row plus one dependency marker (`python_full_version < '3.13'`) that can no longer be true. No package version moved; `uv lock --check` and `uv sync --frozen` both pass. . HOW THE ERROR WAS MADE, which is the part worth keeping. The check was `grep -c 'pyproject.toml' MANIFEST.sha256`, it returned `1`, and `1` was read as "listed". The row it matched belongs to a different file that merely ends with the same name. A substring match answered a question about a path it was never looking at, and returned the shape of a true answer. This is the standing pattern at its sixth instance: the fixture that could not reach the path, the `fatal:` line that failed no check, "the refs moved" mistaken for "the repository works", a guard whose printed remedy could not satisfy it, `git diff` in a bare-flagged repo returning zero for every candidate — and now a grep whose count came from somewhere else entirely. A GREEN VERDICT CAN BE MEASURING THE WRONG THING, and an anchored pattern (`grep -E '  pyproject\.toml$'`) would have said so immediately. . THE REAL COST, WHICH D0191 ALSO DID NOT STATE, and which is why the edit is not free even though it needs no signature: `pyproject.toml` is one of two entries in `HARNESS_FILES` (`src/tannen/laws/harness.py:28`), which feeds `harness_subject` — the descriptor every law is recorded against. Editing it moves ALL 52 law descriptors and stales every evidence record. The price is a full evidence re-run, not an owner's key, and edits that move descriptors should be batched into one re-run rather than paying it per change. . AND THE CLAIM BECOMES CHECKABLE. `tests/test_operating_manual.py` — the file whose whole purpose is comparing what this repository SAYS against what it DOES — gains a detector reading `requires-python` and `.python-version` and refusing any gap between them. It was watched failing against the real tree first, naming 3.12 against 3.13, then passing after the edit. Two fixture-backed negative controls hold it honest in both directions. | accepted | — | public-surface | pytest: `tests/test_operating_manual.py::test_the_declared_python_floor_is_the_interpreter_the_repo_pins`; file: `pyproject.toml` |
| D0195 | C | Three items publication left behind with nowhere to land: a parked cross-repo spec, a frozen CI header that describes a repository that no longer exists, and a policy clause that excludes the push we now make every day | QUEUED FOR THE M3 BOUNDARY SITTING, non-blocking (BRIEF §9.2), joining D0154 by link rather than by edit — the shape that record specifies for itself: "Later M3 items arrive as their own records linking here, never as edits to this one (D0045)." . Filed Tier C for D0154's own stated reason, and because that reason has just been demonstrated again. The digest's "Requires owner" section is a query over TIER-C records. D0191 carried an owner-key item in a Tier-A record and was therefore invisible there — `digest/2026-09-07.md` ends that section at D0176 — and the item survived only because it was rediscovered by hand. (It turned out not to need the owner at all; see D0194. The queue defect is unaffected by that: an item that needs the owner and is filed Tier A is lost whether or not this particular one was.) The three items below all need the owner, and none of them has a queue today. . (1) `SCOPE-under-routing.md` — A CROSS-REPO SPEC IN NO COMMIT, PARKED PENDING A RULING. A 175-line document, mtime 2026-09-06, found in the working tree of `~/git/tannen` during the layout conversion and present in no commit of either the pre- or post-rewrite history. It describes itself as "Companion to: life-agent `DR-DECISION-1-action-space-and-utility.md` §9" and cites as its provenance "decision D-12 of `../life-agent/docs/SESSION-RECORD-2026-09-05.md`". It is parked at `.reference/SCOPE-under-routing.md`, which is gitignored, so it enforces nothing and leaks nothing while it waits. It is deliberately NOT bound as a file below: the path does not exist in a fresh clone or in CI, and a binding that cannot resolve is a broken guard, not a strong one. . Why it is the owner's and not the builder's: it runs directly at the standing rule that no repo of the constellation may depend on another IN EITHER DIRECTION (BRIEF §2's table, §10's non-goals, CLAUDE.md's first hard rule). Whether a scoping document that reasons across the boundary is itself a dependency, and whether tannen may carry one, is a Tier-C question about what the rule means — not a judgement a builder makes by acting. Note also that its own text opens "Repository status note: tannen is private", which has been false since 2026-09-08; a ruling to admit it must correct that line, and a ruling to decline it should say where the document goes instead. . (2) `.github/workflows/ci.yml` DESCRIBES A REPOSITORY THAT NO LONGER EXISTS. Its header reads "This file has never actually run: the repo has no remote (D0061 rationale, and the reason `make verify` on one machine is currently the whole enforcement surface). Adding a remote is a Tier-C door in its own right (external-bytes); when it opens, the justification is …". Every clause is now false: the door opened under D0115/D0176, the remote is `github.com/gfrmin/tannen`, and the file has run three times — failing once (34187597604, which is how D0191 was found) and passing twice. The file is frozen (`MANIFEST.sha256`) and custody-set, so the comment cannot be corrected by a builder even though nothing but prose changes. It is the same class as D0191's `requires-python`: a claim written true, never re-derived, sitting inside the one kind of file that cannot be quietly fixed. It is also now the first thing a public reader meets in the file that tells them how this repository is checked. . (3) `governance/policy.yaml` PERMITS PUSHING TO A PRIVATE ORIGIN AND EXCLUDES EVERY OTHER, AND THIS ORIGIN IS PUBLIC. `in_repo_mechanics.covers` grants Tier A over "pushing to a private origin already configured in this repo", and `in_repo_mechanics.excludes` withholds it from "pushing to any remote other than a private origin already configured here." Read literally, the routine act this repository now performs after every commit is excluded from the tier that authorises it. The authority is real and lies elsewhere — `external_surface.publishing: this-repo-public` plus owner-signed D0115 and D0176 — but the clause that a session actually reads to decide whether it may push says the opposite, and its wording predates publication. `policy.yaml` is owner-signed and named in `required_signatures`, so only the owner can align it. Two shapes to choose between, and the choice is the owner's: widen `covers` to "an origin this repository is published to under `external_surface.publishing`", or delete both clauses and let `external_surface` be the only place that speaks about remotes — one rule in one place, per BRIEF §2. | accepted | — | public-surface, governance-paths | file: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; config: `governance/policy.yaml#in_repo_mechanics.covers`; file: `BRIEF.md` |
| D0196 | A | The M3 custodian draft had gone stale enough to revert the publication sitting, and its own new completeness guard would have turned that revert into a red custody floor at the step where tolerances stop | `docs/proposals/2026-09-04-m3-boundary-sitting/custodian.sh` is REBASED onto the live `scripts/custodian.sh` at HEAD. The draft was written on 2026-09-04 against the then-live file; the publication sitting changed that file twice since (`63428b4`, `6abd071`), and the sitting's step 6 installs the draft by byte-level `diff -q` — so a stale draft is not a stale document, it is a revert with an owner's signature on it. . WHAT INSTALLING IT VERBATIM WOULD HAVE DONE. Three publication-sitting changes reverted: `FOUNDING_TAGS` back to the pre-rewrite pin `531bb8fe…`, which breaks `check_tag_signers`' delegation-precedes-signature epoch against the rewritten tags; the 28-line inline receipt-chain loop restored over D0176's one-line delegation to `scripts/check_receipts.py`, reintroducing exactly the duplication D0183 found rejecting the rewrite attestation; and the three publication poison invocations (`check_concepts_brief_row`, `check_decisions_retired_enforced`, `oracle-shadow-spoofed`) deleted while their fixtures stayed installed on disk. . AND THE THREE INTERACT WITH THE DRAFT'S OWN NEW GUARD, which is the part worth keeping. Hunk 1c adds a completeness pass refusing any installed fixture no invocation exercises. With those three invocations reverted away and their directories still present, the new guard would have `bad`-ed three fixtures — at step 7, which is precisely where `unexpected_failures()` stops tolerating anything and the driver's `custodian --check-only || die` becomes unconditional. The sitting would have died in its irreversible middle, with the owner's key out, holding a custody floor reddened by the guard just installed to strengthen it. A stale draft plus a new derived check is not two small problems. . THE REBASE. Built from the live file forward rather than by patching the old draft, then measured: `diff -u scripts/custodian.sh <draft>` removes exactly seven lines from live, and every one is a line some hunk deliberately replaces. All six hunks are present (1a, 1b, 1c, 2, 3, 4) and every publication-sitting change survives. Verified by running it: `oracle-shadow-model` now fails its poison for `RT-M2-01` — the M2 sitting's own critical fixture, exercised by the custody floor for the first time — the coverage line reports complete, and the floor is intact, in 7.1 seconds. . TWO THINGS THE REBASE FOUND, NEITHER OF WHICH WAS VISIBLE FROM READING. . (a) `prev_head` IS NEVER ASSIGNED ANYWHERE IN THE LIVE CUSTODIAN. Its only occurrence is the `${prev_head:-(none recorded)}` read at `:270`; the loop that used to set it was deleted when the receipt-chain check was delegated out under D0176. So D0154 item (3) is strictly worse than filed: not merely "the chain line is dropped on a same-day re-run" but "every receipt written since the delegation records no previous HEAD at all." `receipts/2026-09-07.md` reads `- previous receipt: 2026-09-03 at (none recorded)`, and no guard noticed because `check_receipts` parses only `- HEAD:`. Hunk 4 fixes both halves — the previous receipt is the latest one that is not the file being written, and its HEAD is read from that file. . (b) THE COMPLETENESS GUARD PRINTED ITS SUCCESS LINE UNCONDITIONALLY. Run against a fabricated orphan fixture, hunk 1c correctly reported the uncovered directory and then closed with "poison coverage: every installed fixture is exercised" anyway. That is D0177's exact shape — a success line that fires regardless of the outcome — reproduced inside the guard written to close D0152's. It is now conditional on the uncovered count. It was caught by running the loop against a fixture no invocation reaches, not by reading it, and the loop had been read several times by then. | accepted | — | governance-paths | file: `docs/proposals/2026-09-04-m3-boundary-sitting/custodian.sh` |

Two processes registering different functions under one name minted one descriptor, one `step_id`, and the second was served the first's output with `rebuilt=False`. `TraceIntegrityError` could not fire because nothing had been tampered with: the recorded output resolved perfectly. A fold is addressed over its operation's source together with its identity and witnesses, and an `AbelianGroup` adds its inverse, which is the whole of the difference between the two aggregate forms. . A name present in a registry but absent from `_CODE` is now refused at declaration, by name: a descriptor that cannot say which code it means is not minted at all. . MEASURED. THE GUARD IS THE FINDING'S OWN DERIVATION, MADE STANDING. For every delta operator, run a two-tick stream twice — once with `replay=True` and once with `replay=False`, the caller feeding integrals to the replaying node and deltas to the maintained one exactly as §7 requires — and collect the operators that diverge or raise. That measured set must equal `_ALWAYS_REPLAYS`. This is D0171 ruling (3)'s "derive AND assert" in its intended shape, and it costs one test in the unsealed `tests/test_incremental.py`. . AN EARLIER SPELLING OF IT WAS VACUOUS IN ONE DIRECTION, and that is worth recording rather than quietly fixing. The first version compared a run under the DECLARED set against a run under an emptied one. For a member wrongly PRESENT that fails correctly; for a member wrongly ABSENT both runs are the maintained one and it passes — so the test could not catch the exact mutation RT-M3-02 is about. The shipped embodiment of §4's contagion rule was pinned by nothing sealed; it is now pinned by a guard that watches it. . A COMPANION ASSERTION, because the derivation is only as good as its input set: the sweep's per-operator stream table is pinned against the package's own `DELTA_OPERATORS`, so adding an operator without a stream fails there first rather than silently shrinking the measured set to match a shrunken declared one. A hand-written table checking a hand-written set would otherwise be the same defect twice. . WHAT IS NOT CLOSED, AND IS THE OWNER'S. Three steps are new (3b, 4k, 4l), four carried defects are fixed, and four rehearsal mechanisms are ported from the publication harness. `scripts/rehearse_sitting.sh` gains the harness half (+181/-9). . TWO OF THE FIXES ARE NOT HOUSEKEEPING — THE DRIVER AS COMMITTED WOULD HAVE STOPPED THIS SITTING, and both were reproduced against the live tree rather than reasoned about. . (1) STEP 5's D0141 RETARGET GUARD FIRES TODAY AND `die`s (D0152 item 1). Its guard asks whether `decisions/0141-*.yaml` still MENTIONS `fixture-candidates/oracle-shadow-model` — and the replacement text this same block writes says "retargeted from docs/redteam/fixture-candidates/oracle-shadow-model/ by that same step". The guard is satisfied by the sentence recording that the work was done, so it re-arms on its own success. Measured: both clauses are true now, and the python then finds `src.count(old) == 0` for the text it means to replace, exits, and reaches `|| die`. That is where both of D0153's concurrent runs stopped. The guard now tests the POST-state — does the record NAME the installed path — which is D0152's own prescribed fix and the shape the step's neighbours already use. D0152 forbids the alternative by name: rewording D0141's detail so the old grep stops matching would make the bug unreproducible without fixing it. . It is the same defect `readme_row_absent()` was written to close, eighty lines earlier in the same step: prose satisfying a grep meant for enforcement. Three instances now live in this one file — step 2's docstring anchor, step 5's README rows, and this. . (2) STEP 6 POINTED AT A CUSTODIAN DRAFT OLDER THAN THE INSTALLED FILE. `$PROPOSALS_M1`, carried forward verbatim from the M1 driver. At M2 that produced a silent skip and left the sitting's own new fixture without its poison line (D0152 item 6). At M3 it is worse than a skip: measured, the live custodian and the M1 draft now differ, so the guard takes the ELSE branch and OFFERS a reversion — `FOUNDING_TAGS` back to its pre-rewrite pin, an inline receipt loop D0176 delegated to `check_receipts.py`, and three publication poison invocations deleted while their fixtures stay on disk. The M3 draft's own hunk 1c would then redden those three at step 7, where tolerances stop and `custodian --check-only || die` is unconditional: the sitting would die in its irreversible middle over a floor its own new guard had reddened. Retargeted to `$PROPOSALS_M3`. . (3) STEP 4f's SKIP-GUARD READ A STRICT SUBSET OF WHAT ITS DECLINE BRANCH REVERTS (D0152 item 2). It grepped `Makefile`; the revert wrote `Makefile`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `tests/test_law_validation.py`. Any state where the first landed and the others did not reads as "already applied" for ever — which is the tree we are in, because a second concurrent run of the driver reverted ci.yml's comment and the subset guard then guaranteed it was never re-offered (D0153 artifact 1). The guard now tests all three, and the apply block is per-file: each edit reports ALREADY / APPLIED / REFUSED, and refuses only a file in neither the pre- nor the post-state, so a partial application is completable rather than skipped. The same edit corrects ci.yml's header, which claims the file has never run and that adding a remote is an unopened Tier-C door (D0195 item 2) — one frozen file, one edit, one manifest row, because two separate edits would leave the second failing its own `count(old) != 1` assertion against bytes the first had changed. . (4) THE SITTING HAD NO LOCK (D0152 item 4). An `flock` on a lockfile keyed to a hash of the worktree path, FD 9 held for the life of the process so the kernel releases it on exit, `die` or kill. Keyed on the worktree because the thing that must not happen twice is two runs against ONE tree; a rehearsal clone has a different path and so a different lock. When `flock(1)` is absent the driver says the guard is NOT ARMED rather than proceeding quietly. . THREE NEW STEPS. 3b offers both of D0195 item (3)'s shapes for `policy.yaml`'s push clause, which grants Tier A over pushing to a PRIVATE origin and excludes every other while this origin is public — the record says the choice is the owner's, so the step does not choose. 4k puts `scripts/rehearse_sitting.sh` in the custody set (RT-M3-06): the driver is custody-set, D0068 makes a green rehearsal its precondition, and the harness that produces that rehearsal is covered by nothing. 4l corrects six passages in `tests/poison/oracle-shadow-model/README.md`, which still opens "**needs patch**" and says it is "staged here and not in tests/poison/" from inside tests/poison/ (D0152 item 5). . FOUR MECHANISMS PORTED FROM THE PUBLICATION HARNESS, and one correction to how they were described. `--abort-at N` is NOT a driver flag and N is not a step number: it lives entirely in the rehearsal harness, where N is a 1-based PROMPT index into the generated answers file. The driver-side knobs are separate — `TANNEN_SITTING_FAST=1` (skip the three long gates and the commit hooks; ~10 minutes instead of two hours) and `TANNEN_SITTING_STOP_AFTER=<step>` (exit 3 after a named step, called after all 24). `say()` now appends every header it prints to a breadcrumb outside the repository, `die()` reads it back to say where it stopped and which of two regimes the tree is in, and the harness reads it too rather than parsing the driver's prose. The harness gains the isolation positive control the boundary side only ever claimed in a comment. . ONE DELIBERATE IMPROVEMENT ON THE PORT. The publication driver spells its fast path `if FAST ... elif confirm ...`, so under FAST the confirm never reads an answer and every later prompt index shifts — which is why its rehearsal mappings all have to be qualified "under TANNEN_SITTING_FAST=1". This driver asks the question in both modes and skips only the work, so an `--abort-at` index means the same thing fast or slow. . AND ONE FAST PATH DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN. `check_decisions` is skipped WHOLE under FAST and the transcript says so. There is no cheap half — measured, its `--help` offers only `--root` and `--today` — and the one environment variable that would shorten it, `TANNEN_CHECK_DECISIONS_NESTED=1`, is RT-08: it disables binding resolution entirely while still printing green. A knob that makes a guard lie is not a fast path. . A FIFTH DEFECT, FOUND BY THE FIRST REHEARSAL AND NOT BY ANY READING OF THE DRIVER. D0199 — written earlier in this same session — binds to `docs/redteam/fixture-candidates/check-laws-dropped-successor/governance/laws.yaml`, and step 5 `git mv`s that tree into `tests/poison/`. The binding stops resolving the instant the fixture lands, which is EXACTLY the shape D0141 had at M2 and which step 5 already carries a retarget block for. Writing a new fixture's record, in the session that also fixed D0141's retarget guard, the same defect was reproduced one record along. . HOW IT SURFACED IS THE INTERESTING PART. The driver's own binding check at the end of step 5 exists to catch precisely this and would have stopped the sitting with "a decision binding stopped resolving when the fixtures moved". Under `TANNEN_SITTING_FAST` that check is skipped whole, so the sitting completed green — and the HARNESS's independent post-condition then failed instead. Two routes to the same fact, and the fast run disabled only one of them. . A SIXTH, IN THE HARNESS, VISIBLE ONLY BECAUSE THE FIFTH FIRED. That post-condition was one check piping `check_decisions` into `grep -q "0 queued"`, so any failure of that guard printed `FAIL no Tier-C door is left unsigned`. All four doors WERE signed; the message sent the reader to `decisions/` to look for an unsigned record that did not exist. It is now two checks from one run — `check_decisions is green` and `no Tier-C door is left queued` — and it prints the offending binding lines by name, because a sitting MOVES files and a binding naming a pre-move path is the recurring shape (D0141 at M2, D0199 at M3). . THE ABORT PORT DOES NOT TRANSFER, AND REHEARSING IT IS WHAT SAID SO. Every confirm in `publication_sitting.sh` is spelled `confirm "..." || die "stopped at your request"`, so one `n` is exit 1 and its harness asserts exactly that. MEASURED in this driver: **zero** confirm sites die on decline; all 42 are `if confirm; then ... else note "declined"; fi`, because declining is a supported answer and every step reverts its own edits. So `--abort-at N` here means DECLINE ONE PROMPT, and a ported verdict asserting exit 1 and `sitting: STOP` would have failed on every run that worked. The verdict now MEASURES the exit status and branches. . There is exactly one prompt that stops this sitting, and only indirectly: declining step 9's commit leaves the tree dirty, and step 10 then refuses to tag over it (D0051, RT-M2-06 D2). Rehearsed at prompt #19 — stopped at step 10, exit 1, tree dirty, `m3-close` not minted. . AND THAT REHEARSAL FOUND THE DEFECT IT EXISTS TO FIND. `die()`'s recovery advice branched on whether step 9 appeared in the breadcrumb, as a proxy for "has committed". Step 9's commit is a confirm the owner may decline, so the run that declined it, was stopped by step 10, and most needed the advice was told: "The sitting had already committed (step 9): the tree is clean and there is nothing to undo" — printed one line under its own `sitting: STOP — the tree is not clean`. Two directly contradictory sentences, in the message an owner reads at the moment they have been stopped. It now asks `git status`, which costs nothing and cannot be wrong about it. THIS IS THE THIRD TIME IN THIS ONE RECORD that a guard tested a proxy instead of the state it cared about (the D0141 guard, step 4f's subset, and now this). . THREE DEFECTS IN THE HARNESS, ALL FOUND BY RUNNING IT AND ALL IN CODE ADDED THIS SESSION. (a) The line added to NAME offending bindings is a bare `grep` under `set -euo pipefail`, so on the first run that had none to name it exited 1 and killed the verdict — printing RC=1 over a run whose every check had passed. The SUCCESS case broke it. (b) The prompt-map awk silently dropped its first group: `prev` is assigned from `$2`, a FIELD, so awk keeps it a "strnum" and comparing it against the string constant `""` coerces both to numbers — step 0's id is literally `0`, so `0 != 0` is false and prompts 1-3 vanished. An operator choosing `--abort-at 2` would have found no step for it. Fixed by concatenating `$2 ""` to force a genuine string, verified against three inputs including a numeric-only step sequence. (c) The transcript scan reported the driver's own expected `sitting: STOP` as an unexpected failure line on every decline run — teaching an operator to skim the one section where the genuinely unexpected shows up. . A FOURTH HARNESS DEFECT, AND THE OLDEST: THE `--answers n` VERDICT ASSERTED THE OPPOSITE OF THE CORRECT OUTCOME. It checked `exit 0` and `no sitting: STOP` for every non-accept run. But declining everything declines step 9's commit, while step 9 runs `gen_projections` and the full custodian UNCONDITIONALLY — they are not confirms, and the custodian writes and signs the receipt — so the tree is necessarily dirty by step 10, where D0051's guard correctly refuses to tag over work no commit contains. A fully declined sitting MUST stop. . That assertion was true when written and was falsified by RT-M2-06 D2, which added the dirty-tree refusal at the M2 boundary; the check was never re-examined, so it has been asserting the wrong outcome ever since. It reported two FAILs against a run that behaved perfectly. Both decline paths now share one `stopped_cleanly()` implementation asserting what a stop must leave behind: it said so, it said where, exit 1, and — on the uncommitted side — a dirty tree, the undo instruction, and no close tag. . A COVERAGE GAP NAMED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER. Every rehearsal run in this session used `--from worktree`, which applies the working tree to the clone as a patch. That is a TRACKED modification, so step 0's clause (a) sets `RESUMED=1` and the precondition gate is skipped — on every run, including the full non-FAST one. Measured in each kept clone: the transcript carries "so this is a RESUMED sitting" and never the gate offer, so step 0's `make verify` branch, and this milestone's FAST arm inside it, have not been executed at all. A green verdict over a skipped step is the exact shape this project keeps rediscovering, so it is recorded here rather than left for a reader to infer from the absence of a line. It closes with a `--from head` run once this work is committed, which is also the state a real sitting starts from. . `VERIFY_ETA` RE-MEASURED (D0154 item 9): `make verify` green end to end in 33m31s over 842 tests, pytest alone 19m16s (840 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xfailed), 2026-09-09. The suite grew 18% since M2 and pytest got FASTER in absolute terms, so the total barely moved — which is why the comment's old framing, "the number only ever grows", is replaced. It would have licensed writing a larger figure without measuring.  . A SEVENTH DEFECT, IN WHAT THE SITTING INSTALLS RATHER THAN IN THE DRIVER — AND THE OBVIOUS FIX FOR IT WAS WRONG. D0199's fixture is the first tree under `tests/poison/` whose payload matches `test_*.py`, and `pyproject.toml` sets `testpaths = ["tests"]` with no `python_files` override. Measured in the kept rehearsal clone: installing it takes the real suite from 842 nodes to 843. The extra node is `test_l1_7_a_law_that_was_retired`, whose body is a docstring, so it passes for free — a permanently green, assertion-free test in the collected suite, in a file whose own docstring says it is "parsed statically and never executed". . RENAMING THE PAYLOAD OUT OF `test_*.py` BREAKS THE FIXTURE SILENTLY. It was drafted, applied, and reverted. `check_laws` finds law DEFINITIONS by globbing `test_*.py`, so the renamed tree defines no laws at all, and the fixture's own documented positive control — `successor: "L1.7"`, a law the tree does define, must return OK — flipped to FAIL. The negative case still failed, still carrying the marker `which no law file defines` that `scripts/custodian.sh` greps for, so the custodian would have gone on printing "guard 'check_laws' fails its poison as required" over a fixture that had stopped testing the successor rule and started testing "this tree contains no law files". One fixture, one reason, collapsed into a tautology that still ticks green. Caught only by running the POSITIVE control the fixture's README documents; the negative control the custodian runs was satisfied throughout. . Excluded structurally instead: `norecursedirs` in `pyproject.toml` now skips any `poison` directory. Measured against the installed layout in the kept clone — 843 back to 842, exactly one node removed and none added. It costs a descriptor move (`pyproject.toml` is in `HARNESS_FILES`, so all 52 laws went STALE and the evidence was regenerated), and it buys the class rather than the instance: the next poison payload will be broken ON PURPOSE, and collecting one is a red suite saying nothing about this repository. . AN EIGHTH, IN THE HARNESS'S REPORTING, WHERE THE TEMPTING FIX WOULD HAVE HIDDEN THE ONE DEFECT THESE REHEARSALS HAVE ACTUALLY CAUGHT. The full run's "unexpected failure lines" section — the section whose stated goal is to be empty — reported `check_decisions: FAIL (3 violation(s))` from step 5. That failure is guaranteed: step 5 installs a poison fixture, so the custody floor is red until step 7 re-signs it, and DECISIONS.md is stale until step 9 regenerates. Adding the line to the position-bounded tolerance list would have silenced it, and it is the SAME LINE D0199's binding defect surfaced on in rehearsal 1. The harness now asserts the block carries those three known violations and nothing else, and suppresses the line only while that assertion holds. Verified both ways against the kept transcript, including a doctored copy carrying rehearsal 1's actual D0199 violation: it is named, the check goes red, and the line stays visible. . THE FULL NON-FAST REHEARSAL IS GREEN (2026-09-09). Driver exit 0 in 100 minutes; harness total 144m43s; all 18 verdict checks ok; zero unexpected failure lines. Both `make verify` gates ran in full — 841 passed / 1 skipped / 1 xfailed, 18m12s at step 9 and 18m49s at step 11 — with no `TANNEN_SITTING_FAST` marker anywhere in the transcript. `m3-close` minted at step 10 and verified as owner@tannen, custody set re-signed, receipt taken before the tag. One correction to how the sitting was described earlier in this record: it makes TWO commits, not one — step 9's and step 11's — so an owner should budget two rounds of pre-commit hooks. . A NINTH AND A TENTH, BOTH FOUND BY THE ONE RUN THAT STARTS FROM A COMMITTED TREE. Every rehearsal before 2026-09-09 ran `--from worktree`, which applies the working tree as a patch; that is a tracked modification, so step 0's clause (a) set RESUMED=1 and SKIPPED the precondition gate on all four green runs. A gate that has never executed is not covered by any number of green verdicts over it. `--from head` closes that, and could only run once this work was committed (head mode does not copy untracked files) — which is also the order the owner will use. . THE NINTH is that `--from head` rehearses the WRONG DRIVER unless told otherwise. In worktree mode the harness picks up the working tree's driver; in head mode it takes the committed `scripts/boundary_sitting.sh`, still byte-identical to the M2 copy. The first attempt printed "driver under test: scripts/boundary_sitting.sh, unmodified since HEAD" and was rehearsing M2. The harness passes the milestone as an argument, so MILESTONE would have been right and only the $PROPOSALS_M2 paths wrong — D0152 item 6 exactly, in the run convened to close a coverage gap, and it could well have gone green. `TANNEN_REHEARSE_DRIVER` is the override; the run was killed and relaunched with it, confirmed by "(OVERRIDDEN)" in the transcript. Documented in the proposal README rather than defaulted, because a harness that guesses which driver you meant is the same defect one layer up. . THE TENTH is what the precondition gate says the first time it runs: `check_manifest: FAIL (1 violation(s))`, one violation, "custody drift: scripts/boundary_sitting.sh changed since the custody file was written". This is not a defect in the driver — it is the truth. The driver under test has just been copied over a custody-set member and is deliberately not re-signed until step 7, and the driver answers "green except the custody set, which is this sitting's step 7 — continuing". THE OWNER'S OWN `cp` PRODUCES THE SAME LINE, so a real sitting shows it too, and the proposal README now lists it among the expected non-fatal lines. The defect was in the harness's reporting: it landed in the section whose goal is to be empty. Named, not tolerated, on the D0199 precedent — the block must carry that one drift and nothing else, and an injected "frozen path BRIEF.md does not match its manifest hash" was watched being caught, named, and disarming the suppression. . AND A SIXTH INSTANCE OF THE CLASS THIS MILESTONE KEEPS PRODUCING: both tolerances, as first written, pass when the failure they tolerate is simply absent. A run that never reached the gate would report the same green as one that examined a real block and found it clean — a guard measuring a proxy rather than the state. Each block now counts its input first and prints which case it is in, the same remedy as the RESUMED note. . THE `--from head` REHEARSAL IS GREEN (2026-09-09). 20/20 verdict checks ok, RC=0, 146m36s, RESUMED=0 with the precondition gate exercised for the first time, and zero unexpected failure lines once the tenth defect above was named. Three `make verify` legs rather than two, which is the whole cost difference against the 144m43s worktree run. `m3-close` minted and verified as owner@tannen; the real repository's HEAD and working tree unchanged, checked before and after by root_state(). Recorded here verbatim in substance and UNSIGNED, on D0171's precedent and for D0171's stated reason: the rulings are instructions the builder acts on immediately where the act is reversible, and the Tier-C half — composing the sitting, narrowing the custody set, superseding frozen prose — is authoritative only once this record carries the owner's signature at a sitting. A record of rulings is not the key that enacts them (D0063), and a Tier-C record without a signature is not accepted (D0064). . THE REVIEW'S CENTRAL OBSERVATION, recorded because it is the reason the rulings exist and it generalises past this milestone: "every boundary, the ceremony grows because the previous ceremony's defects justified new guards, and each addition was individually correct. That is a ratchet with no release." The M3 driver is 26 steps and ~100 minutes, a full rehearsal 146, and the boundary needs two rehearsals plus the run — roughly six and a half hours of ceremony for one milestone. The owner's framing: "you are now maintaining two systems, and only one of them is tannen." . (1) COMMISSION A FLOOR-SIMPLIFICATION AUDIT, Session-A shaped, TAKING PRECEDENCE OVER FURTHER DRIVER HARDENING. Which custody guards, receipt-chain mechanics and history-integrity checks are made redundant by a protected remote with required signature verification, now that the remote is public? Target: a smaller custody set and a shorter ceremony. The owner's argument: "that's the one change that removes mechanism instead of adding it, and it's now available where it wasn't at M0." DONE — see D0202 and `docs/proposals/2026-09-04-m3-boundary-sitting/FLOOR-AUDIT.md`. (2) SPLIT THE CEREMONY BY CONSEQUENCE. A short signing ceremony for the irreversible acts — custody re-signature, close tag, Tier-C signatures — with the reversible batch applied and verified beforehand by the builder under existing delegation. "If the reason that can't happen is that fixtures live in author-key territory, then the right fix is to narrow the custody set to what actually needs the key, which is the same audit as (1)." ANSWERED BY THE AUDIT, and not in the direction the ruling anticipated: the blocker is not custody-set membership and narrowing the set is refused, but the ceremony still shortens by ~35 minutes and one owner signature per boundary via a different route (D0202). . (3) DRAFT THE TWO DEFERRED SESSION-A ITEMS BEFORE M4 SESSION A rather than letting them roll again: the falsified passages in `docs/specs/m3.md` (superseded forward under the D0128 mechanism), and the package-qualified import in the frozen M3 law files — the latter now recommended at THREE consecutive boundaries. The owner's reason, which is D0171 ruling (1)'s reason restated: "frozen prose known to be false is precisely how D0049 happened." IN PROGRESS as builder drafting; installation stays owner territory. . (4) D0148 ITEM 5 IS RULED, after four boundaries in the queue as a pure judgement call: MOVE THE RECEIPT BEHIND THE COMMIT CONFIRM. The owner's argument: "a signed receipt for a sitting that was abandoned attests to presence at something that did not happen, which is worse than reordering the receipt-then-tag argument." Measured at `docs/proposals/2026-09-04-m3-boundary-sitting/boundary_sitting.sh:2523-2543`: step 9 runs `custodian.sh`, which writes AND SIGNS `receipts/<date>.md`, three commands BEFORE the `confirm "Commit the sitting so far?"` at :2539. Decline that prompt and the signed receipt already exists. . RULING (4)'s CORRECT IMPLEMENTATION IS TO MOVE THE CONFIRM EARLIER, NOT THE RECEIPT LATER, and the distinction is load-bearing. Moving the receipt after the COMMIT would leave it outside the commit that step 10's close tag attests, so the tag would name a commit not containing the receipt. Moving it after the CONFIRM keeps the receipt inside the commit, keeps it ahead of the close tag — so D0071's receipt-then-tag argument survives intact and only the receipt-versus-commit order changes — and yields no receipt at all on a declined sitting, which is the whole point. . RULING (4)'s EDGE CASE, PUT TO THE OWNER AND ANSWERED 2026-09-09: a sitting whose every step is already a no-op leaves the tree clean, so a commit-gated receipt would never be taken. Asked whether an owner attending a no-op sitting should still get a receipt, the owner ruled NO — "a receipt needs an act". The dirty-tree test therefore gates both the commit and the receipt, and a quiet boundary lets the receipt clock go stale, which under BRIEF §9.1 blocks Tier-B work until the next sitting that does something. That consequence is intended, not incidental. . (5) REHEARSAL OF THE M3 DRIVER AS IT STANDS: PROCEED. "The ceremony ships as built for this boundary; the simplification lands before M4's." The rehearsal is already complete — five paths green, D0200 — so this ruling reads as: do not hold the M3 boundary for the audit or the simplification. THE BUILDER'S READING OF (4) AGAINST (5), stated so the owner can refuse it: ruling (4) settles the judgement and this record discharges its "record the reordering against D0071 explicitly" instruction, but the driver is NOT edited for this boundary, because any edit voids the five-path certification at a cost of ~146 minutes of re-rehearsal and ruling (5) says the ceremony ships as built. The change lands with the ruling (1)/(2) rework, which restructures step 9 regardless. The residual risk accepted by that reading, stated plainly: if the M3 sitting is abandoned after step 9's custodian run, a signed receipt will attest to a sitting that did not complete. If the owner would rather pay the re-rehearsal, the change is small and specified above. . THREE CLAIMS IN THE REVIEW ARE CORRECTED, because a ruling recorded on a false premise propagates. (a) "The design target was five minutes a week" — THERE IS NO WEEKLY MINUTE FIGURE ANYWHERE IN THIS REPOSITORY. Searched at HEAD and at `brief-freeze` across BRIEF, policy, decisions, docs and DELEGATIONS. The accretion complaint stands on `governance/policy.yaml:48-49` instead — "deference spends owner attention, which is the one resource the autonomy protocol exists to conserve" — which is a firmer footing than an invented target. (b) "The driver now has 24 steps" — it has TWENTY-SIX (`grep -c '^say "Step '`), and this record's own proposal README repeated the 24 at :187 while its live/no-op split at :219-220 sums to 25. | D0202 | A | Publication gave the floor a second observer and substitutes for no local guard: thirty-five substitution claims, zero survivors, and the ceremony shortens by a different route | THE FLOOR-SIMPLIFICATION AUDIT COMMISSIONED BY D0201 RULING (1) RETURNS A NULL RESULT ON THE CUSTODY SET. Seven mechanism families were surveyed — the custody set, the custodian's guards, the receipt chain, history integrity, GitHub's actual capability, the ceremony split by consequence, and the constitutional constraints — and every redundancy claim was then attacked by an independent reviewer instructed to default to "refuted" when uncertain. THIRTY-FIVE CLAIMS WERE RAISED AND THIRTY-FIVE WERE REFUTED. No member of the custody set is removed. The full audit is `docs/proposals/2026-09-04-m3-boundary-sitting/FLOOR-AUDIT.md`. . THE PREMISE WAS PARTLY COUNTERFACTUAL AND THAT MATTERS. Measured 2026-09-09: `GET /repos/gfrmin/tannen/branches/master/protection` returns 404, `GET .../rulesets` returns `[]`, `commit.gpgsign=false`, and every commit reports `%G? = N`. A protected remote with required signature verification is unbuilt work, not a facility to spend against. . AND IF IT WERE BUILT IT WOULD VERIFY A DIFFERENT TRUST ROOT. GitHub's "Verified" badge attests that a signature matches a key registered to a GitHub ACCOUNT. This repository's trust root is `ssh-keygen -Y verify -f allowed_signers` against two deliberately distinct principals, `builder@tannen` and `owner@tannen` (D0015), separated so that an author-signed artifact "verifies only against `owner@tannen`, so a builder signature can never satisfy it" (`allowed_signers:3-5`). One GitHub account pushes both roles; GitHub cannot tell them apart and has no notion of the namespaces — `tannen-custody`, `tannen-policy`, `tannen-decision`, `tannen-receipt`, `tannen-rewrite` — that separate presence from authorisation. Substituting the one for the other is what BRIEF §9.1's "authorisation attaches to the artifact of record, never to a report about it" forbids. . THERE IS ALSO A STRUCTURAL BAR, and it is the repository's own: D0063 ruling (3), quoted at `scripts/custodian.sh:18-25` — "THE FLOOR MAY DEPEND ONLY ON TOOLS THE OS PROVIDES AND PATHS NAMED LITERALLY." `gh` is not OS-provided, requires a credential, and returns a third party's assertion. A remote may be a second observer; it may not become a term in the floor's verdict. The binding vocabulary makes the same point in paperwork: any in-repo assertion about branch protection can only be `documentary`, so relying on a remote control converts an enforced binding into one that detects nothing. . THE DECISIVE FACT IS THAT NOTHING PUSHES. `grep -rn 'git push' scripts/ Makefile` returns nothing, and the boundary driver has no push step. The sitting signs the custody set, the receipt and the close tag against a local working tree the remote has never seen, so the window in which the ceremony's every irreversible act occurs is precisely the window no remote can witness. Four further attack families survive any remote configuration: local ref deletion is not a remote event (`git tag -d brief-freeze` pushes nothing, and empties `bless_epoch` at `scripts/custodian.sh:81-83`); a tree-content attack is a legal fast-forward that satisfies every proposed rule while deleting `Makefile:44`, the only path by which the custodian runs; the topic-branch launder rewrites an unprotected milestone branch and merges forward, leaving master append-only; and a trust-root re-issue can carry a genuinely valid signature, caught only by the object-hash pin at `governance/tag-roles.yaml:16-19`. Finally, offline third-party verification is the stated point of publishing (D0176): a clone contains no protection state at all, so every guard removed on the strength of a remote control is a guard a stranger loses entirely — and a control the constrained party can switch off from this machine's own keyring is not a trust root. . THE CEREMONY SHORTENS ANYWAY, BY A ROUTE THE RULING DID NOT ANTICIPATE. The blocker on D0201 ruling (2)'s split is not custody-set membership, so narrowing the set would not have bought it. Owner attention is ~55 minutes of the ~100-minute run and should not shrink — step 8 alone is 600 lines of Tier-C records read in full, which is the attention the protocol exists to spend. The clock is elsewhere: two `make verify` legs at 18m12s and 18m49s in the rehearsal clone, and pre-commit rounds at ~12 minutes each. The recommended cut is to DERIVE `required_tags` from the boundary tags instead of maintaining it by hand (`governance/tag-roles.yaml:47-55`, read at `scripts/check_tag_signers.py:151`) — which is D0095 half (2), still "applied by NOTHING", and honours D0171 ruling (3)'s standing rule against hand-maintained enumerations. Deriving it DELETES STEP 11 of every future sitting, and with it one verify leg, one hook round, one commit, and the second of the two owner custody signatures: ~100 minutes to ~55-65, and four owner signature moments instead of five, for ever, with no guard removed. . ONE ADDITION TO THE CUSTODY SET IS RECOMMENDED, WIDENING RATHER THAN NARROWING: `scripts/rehearse_sitting.sh` (RT-M3-06, already drafted as the driver's step 4k). It is the harness whose green output is D0068's precondition for the real sitting, it is in neither `MANIFEST.sha256` nor the custody set, and it already writes `owner@tannen` lines into a clone's `allowed_signers` — one `$CLONE`-for-`$ROOT` slip launders the trust root with every gate green. . ONE RECOMMENDATION IS REFUSED AND THE REFUSAL IS THE POINT. Moving driver steps 4f and 4k into builder pre-work between sittings would require narrowing `governance/policy.yaml:62-63`, the clause forbidding builder edits to frozen or signed files. That clause is strictly broader than BRIEF door 5 and is the genuine release valve on offer — but the pre-commit frozen-path hook currently PREVENTS those edits, and after narrowing a guard-weakening edit would be live until someone noticed, with a stale custody signature as detection rather than prevention. The payback is four prompts and under five minutes. That trade is refused. | accepted | — | governance-paths, public-surface | file: `docs/proposals/2026-09-04-m3-boundary-sitting/FLOOR-AUDIT.md`; file: `governance/tier-c.yaml`; file: `governance/tag-roles.yaml`; file: `scripts/rehearse_sitting.sh` |

Eight claims across four angles were raised and adversarially attacked; as in the main audit, all eight were refuted. The section is appended to the audit as §8 and the answer is summarised here. . THE FRAMING IS OFF BY SIX SIGNATURES. "Before the signing window" has no referent inside the ceremony: the owner's key is first used at STEP 3 on `governance/policy.yaml`, again at step 3b, twice in step 4c and once in step 4h — six owner-key signature sites before step 7's custody signature. The only point genuinely before the window is step 0, whose tree is the pre-sitting HEAD. . AND THERE IS NOTHING TO PUSH. The driver has exactly two commit sites, both after step 7: step 9 and step 11. Every act of steps 0-8b writes uncommitted working-tree state, and `git push` moves refs and objects, not a working tree. This is structural rather than incidental — each artifact is signed as a byte string at the moment it is written, so the signature precedes any commit that could carry it. . MANUFACTURING SOMETHING TO PUSH IS REFUSED ONE LAYER EARLIER, BY A RULE THE OWNER HAS ALREADY DECLINED TO BEND. A non-empty pre-signing push requires adding a commit to the irreversible middle, and that commit cannot be taken: `.pre-commit-config.yaml` runs `check_manifest.py`, whose `main()` calls `check_custody` unconditionally BEFORE the `--staged` branch, and `check_custody` fails on precisely the drift the ceremony creates by construction. Forcing it needs `--no-verify`, which D0181 refused for a real commit even under a direct owner ruling. If it were forced, `git add -A` would sweep that drift into public history and `ci.yml` — `on: push:`, no branch filter — would publish a red verdict on the ceremony's middle while the owner was still sitting. . ONE VARIANT SURVIVES STRUCTURALLY AND IS REFUSED ON THE ABORT PATH. A push at the seam between step 9's commit and step 10's tag needs no invented commit and no red floor. It is refused because it would be the ceremony's first published act, and the two failures immediately downstream — the owner declining the close tag, and `verify-tag` failing after `git tag -s` succeeded — would strand a never-closed sitting on public `master`. Today no abort leaves anything beyond this machine. The refusal is therefore a price, not an impossibility, and the price is the abort path. . THE FINDING THAT RUNS THE OTHER WAY IS THE USEFUL ONE, AND IT IS QUEUED. The audit's §3(a) makes an attack family conditional on ignorance: a pre-push rewrite "is invisible to a remote that has not received the prior state." Pushing the pre-sitting HEAD BEFORE the ceremony delivers exactly that state and closes family (a) — the only one of the six a remote can close. That is not a reordering; it is ordinary builder habit performed beforehand. AND NOTHING ENFORCES IT: measured 2026-09-10, the driver contains zero occurrences of `git fetch`, `git push`, `ls-remote` or any remote-tracking ref, `docs/SITTING.md` uses the words push, origin and remote zero times, and no guard consults a remote. The property was FALSE for over twenty-seven hours on 2026-09-09 by this repository's own reflog — `origin/master` sat at `2bb4954` from 15:10 on 2026-09-08 until 18:55 the next day, which is the window the audit was written in and the state §3(a) describes. The recommendation is one comparison at step 0: the sitting refuses to start unless `origin` already holds HEAD. . IT IS NOT LANDED, AND THE REASON IS THE OWNER'S OWN. It is an ADDITION to the ceremony, and the standing objection of 2026-09-09 is exactly to additions that are each individually correct — "that's a ratchet with no release." Whether a boundary sitting may depend on the network at all is the owner's call: it would be the first step of the ceremony that fails when the network does. Queued to the boundary with the rest. . A LIVE DEFECT WAS FOUND ON THE WAY AND IS FIXED HERE. Asking what a mid-ceremony push would strand exposed what the ceremony already strands. `die()` branched on `git status --porcelain` alone, and the working tree was never a complete account of a sitting: a minted, owner-signed close tag lives outside it. FOUR `die()` sites are downstream of `git tag -s` — `verify-tag`, and step 11's projection, custodian and `make verify` failures, the last much the likeliest — and step 10 has just required the tree to be clean, so all four printed "nothing is half-applied. This is a coherent place to stop" over a signed close tag. The rehearsal harness could not catch it either: its `<milestone>-close was NOT minted` assertion sat inside the DIRTY branch, unreachable in exactly the case that matters. The driver now asks the refs before the tree and says what the run left behind; the harness asks the tag question on every abort, in both branches, and the negative case is a note rather than a check because the branch condition has already decided it. | accepted | — | governance-paths, public-surface | file: `docs/proposals/2026-09-04-m3-boundary-sitting/FLOOR-AUDIT.md`; file: `docs/proposals/2026-09-04-m3-boundary-sitting/boundary_sitting.sh`; file: `scripts/rehearse_sitting.sh` |
| D0211 | A | D0171 ruling (2) keeps its outcome and loses its reason: the type system catches nothing here, and the executor answers the swap from the trace | D0171 ruling (2)'s STATED PREMISE IS FALSE, and this record carries the correction so the ruling can be signed without signing the reason. Owner ruling of 2026-09-10, asked and answered before the sitting: "amend the premise, then sign." . The amendment is THIS RECORD and not an edit to D0171, because D0045 makes `decision` and `rationale` immutable and states no exception for an unsigned record — "a change of mind is a NEW record". The M3 driver's own step-8 note says amending "costs nothing now and costs a supersession after", which reads as licence to edit in place; measured against D0045 it is not, and the distinction it is reaching for is real but narrower: before signature a correction is a plain record, after signature it is a supersession of signed bytes. . WHAT IS FALSE. Ruling (2) accepts order-insensitive `derivation_id` on the ground that operand order is "a caller error the type system should catch, not the identity scheme." RT-M3-03 tested the premise rather than the conclusion. Give both relations the same schema and there is nothing to catch: `anti_join(A, B)` and `anti_join(B, A)` are different questions, both legal, and they share one `step_id` (`sha256:7e1fc9687080dbd8590c87ad345b6bc4f1e81598da1e91433097281c2f6f6a21`). The second call returns the FIRST call's answer with `rebuilt=False` — the wrong result served as a cache hit, no exception raised. With a fresh trace store the same call returns `[]` correctly, so the trace is what corrupts it. This is RT-M3-01's disease in a second place. . WHAT STANDS. The ruling's OUTCOME is unchanged and is not weakened by the correction: `derivation_id` stays order-insensitive and is not widened at M4. Widening it does invalidate evidence across three milestones, and that price is real. The corrected ground is that THE ASYMMETRY BELONGS TO THE OPERATOR, NOT TO THE IDENTITY SCHEME — not that a type system intercepts it, which it demonstrably does not. . WHAT IS QUEUED, NOT DECIDED HERE. RT-M3-03's remedy is M4 work and needs a frozen law, so it is named rather than taken: either fold role-named operands (`{"left": …, "right": …}`) into the derivation for a non-commutative operator, so two orders are two derivations because they are two different input values, or have `advance` refuse a bare positional pair for such an operator. Either leaves m1 §8, L1.13 and every existing `deltaop/1` descriptor untouched. . AND ONE CONSTRAINT ON THAT REMEDY, from D0171's own ruling (3): the set of non-commutative binary operators is today exactly `{anti_join}` — `union` and `join` are genuinely commutative, so order-insensitivity is correct for them and the blanket rule is wrong only for `anti_join`. That set MUST BE DERIVED, not written down. A hand-maintained list here would be the next instance of the class ruling (3) was made to stop. | accepted | — | — | file: `docs/redteam/2026-09-05-m3-boundary.md`; file: `decisions/0171-the-m3-conferral-rulings.yaml`; pytest: `tests/test_incremental.py::test_a_binary_step_id_inherits_derivation_ids_order_insensitivity` |
| D0212 | C | D0195 item 1 ruled: a scoping document that reasons across the constellation boundary is a dependency, and tannen does not carry one | DECLINED. Owner ruling of 2026-09-10, asked and answered before the M3 sitting: `.reference/SCOPE-under-routing.md` does not belong in tannen. It belongs in life-agent. . D0195 item 1 put the question the right way round — not "is this file harmful?" but "is a scoping document that reasons across the boundary itself a dependency, and may tannen carry one?" The ruling is that it is, and tannen may not. The document describes itself as "Companion to: life-agent `DR-DECISION-1-action-space-and-utility.md` §9" and cites as its provenance "decision D-12 of `../life-agent/docs/SESSION-RECORD-2026-09-05.md`". A companion to another repo's decision record, deriving from another repo's session record, is that repo's artifact wherever the bytes happen to sit. CLAUDE.md's first hard rule and BRIEF §2/§10 say IN EITHER DIRECTION, and the direction that is easy to miss is this one: tannen holding a document that only makes sense beside life-agent's is tannen depending on life-agent, not the reverse. . WHERE IT GOES: life-agent, which owns both documents it names. This ruling does not place it there — writing into another repo of the constellation is not an act this repo authorises itself to take, and the relocation is the owner's, performed in life-agent's own history. . WHAT THE SITTING DOES ABOUT IT: nothing, and that is not an oversight. The file is gitignored and present in no commit of either the pre- or post-rewrite history, so there is nothing to remove from tannen's record and nothing for a step of the driver to do. The enacting act is the deletion of one untracked file from the working tree of `~/git/tannen` once a copy is safe in life-agent. Deliberately NOT bound as a `file` binding below: the path does not exist in a fresh clone or in CI, and D0195 is right that a binding which cannot resolve is a broken guard rather than a strong one. . ONE CORRECTION THAT TRAVELS WITH IT: the document's line 11 reads "Repository status note: tannen is private. It does not appear in any public-master…", false since 2026-09-08. On an admission that line would have had to be fixed as a condition. On a decline it is life-agent's to fix, and it is named here so the error does not simply move house unremarked. | accepted | — | — | file: `decisions/0195-three-items-publication-left-with-no-queue-to-land-in.yaml`; file: `CLAUDE.md` |
| D0213 | A | The M3 sitting's first builder follow-up: seventeen bindings upgraded across eleven Tier-A records, the poison suite wired to the fixture the sitting installed, and nine upgrades that stop at a signature | THE FIRST TWO OF THE THREE FOLLOW-UPS THE M3 BOUNDARY SITTING NAMED AT ITS CLOSE, both Tier A and neither needing a signature: upgrade the bindings the sitting made enforceable, and add the fixture it installed to tests/test_governance_scripts.py. D0045 is what makes the first legal — a record's decision is immutable and its bindings are not, because "attaching one when that artifact finally exists records history rather than rewriting it". . SEVENTEEN BINDINGS ACROSS ELEVEN RECORDS: thirteen raised from documentary to enforced, seven of those also hardened from `file` to `manifest`, plus four new bindings. Five were waiting on custodian hunks the sitting installed (D0146 hunk 3, D0152 hunks 2/1a/1b, D0153 hunk 4, D0172 hunk 1c, D0177 hunk 2); one on `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s corrected header and one on `tests/poison/oracle-shadow-model/README.md`, whose title said "needs patch" for a whole milestone after the patch had shipped (both D0152); three on `scripts/rehearse_sitting.sh` joining the custody set (D0149, D0150, D0202 — RT-M3-06); one on the M3 driver replacing the M2 one at `scripts/boundary_sitting.sh` (D0152); and two on `tests/poison/README.md`, whose missing row landed at the M2 sitting on 2026-09-03 and which nobody upgraded for a milestone (D0122, D0140). . WHERE THE TYPE MOVED, IT MOVED FOR A MECHANISM. A `file` binding resolves by bare existence, so it enforces nothing whatever its strength says; `file` became `manifest` wherever the target carries a MANIFEST.sha256 row, because that row is what turns a revert into a red check_manifest — `make verify`'s first recipe line — rather than a change nobody can see. Two targets are custody-set but not manifested (`scripts/boundary_sitting.sh`, `scripts/rehearse_sitting.sh`): they keep `type: file` and say so in the binding, because what detects a revert there is check_custody's drift line and no binding type names the custody set. . NINE MORE WERE PREPARED, MEASURED, AND REVERTED — they are the owner's, and D0214 queues them. A Tier-C record's signature is over the file's whole bytes, so editing its bindings invalidates it: after the nine edits, all five affected records failed `ssh-keygen -Y verify` with `incorrect signature`, and check_decisions would have failed each as "Tier-C record accepted without an owner signature". check_decisions.py:384-390 says this outright and has since RT-06 — "a later binding change costs a re-signature: what was vouched for is the file, not a summary of it". What no artifact says is the consequence for this follow-up: the driver's closing note asks the builder to upgrade the bindings the sitting made enforceable, and roughly a third of them cannot be reached without the key that just left the room. . THE FIXTURE THE SITTING INSTALLED IS NOW IN THE SUITE TOO. `check-laws-dropped-successor/` was installed at step 5 and wired into the custodian by hunk 5 in the same commit, and reached `tests/test_governance_scripts.py` only afterwards, by hand — this record's own work. It is now POISON row `check_laws`, and beside it a derived completeness pass that walks `tests/poison/*/` and fails for any fixture no row and no dedicated test exercises, and for any name the suite claims that is not installed. That is custodian hunk 1c reached from plain `uv run pytest`, which is this file's own stated reason for existing: CI and a builder run the suite many times a day and run the custodian at sittings. . FIVE UPGRADES WERE CONSIDERED AND REFUSED, each because the reason the binding gives is still true, and refusing them is the point of grading strength at all. `governance/policy.yaml#in_repo_mechanics.covers` (D0195) had its false push clause deleted at the sitting, but the clause is still read by sessions and by no guard. `governance/tag-roles.yaml` under D0171 ruling (3), D0172 finding (C), D0202 and D0205 stays documentary because `required_tags` is complete, not derived, and the derivation is deferred to M4. `docs/specs/m3.md` (D0171 ruling (1)) stays documentary because the frozen file still holds the false sentence by design — what carries the correction is D0204, not an edit. `governance/policy.yaml#licence_defaults` (D0184) stays documentary for the reason it was written with. And D0172 finding (G), the poison README table nothing checks, stays open and is expected to: the only way to check that table is to read its prose, and no test here may learn another artifact's state that way. | accepted | — | governance-paths | pytest: `tests/test_governance_scripts.py::test_guard_fails_its_poison[check_laws]`; pytest: `tests/test_governance_scripts.py::test_every_installed_fixture_is_exercised_by_this_suite`; file: `tests/test_governance_scripts.py` |
