| D0215 | C | Minting the close tag reddens the commit it attests: DECISIONS.md's attention-receipt line is computed from tags and the clock, and a commit can contain neither | QUEUED FOR THE M4 BOUNDARY SITTING, non-blocking (BRIEF §9.2). It joins D0214, which opened that queue. . THE FINDING, MEASURED: every close tag this project has minted points at a commit that fails `make verify` today, and the tag itself is what fails it. . (1) m1-close points at c13d33c, m2-close at 805a301, m3-close at e33adf8. All three of those commits carry the same shape of line in DECISIONS.md: "Attention receipt: **FRESH** — receipt <date>.md fresh (no milestone boundary since)". (2) check_decisions.py:459 compares that line against the verdict the current run computes. The computation is scripts/_gov.py:300-306, whose `later` list comes from boundary_tag_dates() at :211 — a shell-out to `git tag -l`. Tags are refs. No commit contains one. (3) So the instant step 10 mints the close tag, the line inside the commit step 10 has just tagged becomes false, and stays false for good. . MEASURED ON M3 RATHER THAN INFERRED. CI run 34481481487 on e33adf8 failed with exactly that violation, plus six pytest-binding failures downstream of it (D0063 and D0177 on tests/test_governance_scripts.py; D0050, D0054, D0058 and D0062 on tests/test_tag_signers.py — all innocent, all reporting the same stale projection). Run 34481481603 on a285f93, the very next commit, passed. e33adf8's own pre-commit hooks were green when it was made: the sitting could not have continued past step 9 otherwise. The commit did not change. The tag set did. . THE SCOPE IS WIDER THAN THE TAG, and this is the part that costs. A commit is red on this comparison whenever the verdict stored in its DECISIONS.md differs from the one its own receipts yield against today's tags and today's date. There are two ways for that to happen and between them they cover nearly all of history. (i) The stored line says "no milestone boundary since" and a boundary tag dated on or after that commit's newest receipt has since been minted. BOUNDARY_TAG_RE at _gov.py:25 matches brief-freeze, *-laws-freeze and *-close, so this is true of every commit older than m3-close whose newest receipt predates 2026-09-10. (ii) The stored line says "fresh until D" and today is past D — true of every commit more than seven days behind its own boundary, from _gov.py:304. So `git bisect run make verify`, the ordinary way to locate a regression in this repo, fails immediately on a governance line for every commit outside a narrow window near the tip, and says nothing whatever about the code being bisected. . CONTROL, run for this record and predicted before it was read. af41fe8 is not a sitting commit at all — it is the ordinary commit before the sitting — and CI run 34434680220 passed on it on 2026-09-10. Its tree's newest receipt is 2026-09-07 and m3-close is dated 2026-09-10, so case (i) says the same run, re-run byte-identical on 2026-09-11, must now fail computing "receipt 2026-09-07.md fresh until 2026-09-17 (boundary 2026-09-10 + 7d)" against a stored "receipt 2026-09-07.md fresh (no milestone boundary since)". IT DID, at 00:18:33Z on 2026-09-11, and the guard printed that string character for character: check_decisions FAIL, 3 violations — the attention-receipt line plus D0063 and D0177's pytest bindings, the same two innocents the M3 sitting's own failure dragged with it. Nothing about af41fe8 changed between the two runs. m3-close was minted in between. Greenness here is not a property of a commit. . THE RECOMMENDATION: stop storing a time-varying verdict in a projection that must match a recomputation. DECISIONS.md should carry only what its commit contains — the latest receipt's filename and whether it is signed — and the FRESH/STALE verdict, which has a clock in it, should be rendered where a dated artifact can carry it honestly: digest/<date>.md, which is generated per day and is never compared against a later recomputation. check_decisions goes on computing the verdict and reporting it at run time; it stops asserting that a tracked file agrees with it. That preserves what RT-M2-05 asked for (no file may go on claiming FRESH after the receipt goes stale) by removing the claim from the file that cannot keep it, rather than by checking it harder. | blocked-on-owner | — | governance-paths | file: `scripts/_gov.py`; file: `scripts/check_decisions.py`; file: `scripts/boundary_sitting.sh` |
